SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 2, Special Branch.
REPORT
Date. May 11th 1934.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No. S.B. REGISTRY.
No. D. 5867
Date. 11 / 5 / 34

Subject (in full) Lewis D. Carson, applicant for S.M.P. (Specials).

Made by. D.S. Pitts Forwarded by. J.B. King. D.C.

With reference to the attached application from one
Lewis D. Carson, American, for enrolment in the S.M.P. (Specials),
I have to report that nothing is known to this gentleman's
detriment from a Police point of view, whilst careful enquiries
indicate that he is an individual fit in all respects for the
type of work undertaken by the S.M.P. (Specials).

J.A. Pitts.
D. S.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

Subject (in full)...Twenty-one applicants for enrolment in S.M.P. (Specials).

Made by. D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by. J.B.Ku. D.C.

With reference to the following twenty-one applicants for
enrolment in the S.M.P. (Specials):-
(1) Rudolf Pasche, German.
(2) John Thomas, British.
(3) Robert H. Shrap, Austrian.
(4) H. Engemann, German.
(5) Andreas Gatz, German.
(6) Max Dahl, German.
(7) J. H. Klansz, Netherlander.
(8) Charles Specht, German.
(9) J. G. Shand, British.
(10) M. H. Iochvidoff (Known as M. H. Duff), Russian.
(11) E. A. Cooke, British.
(12) J. H. Campbell, British.
(13) R. Marcal, Portuguese.
(14) C.A.B. Silva, Portuguese.
(15) J. N. Ribeiro, Portuguese.
(16 ) O.H. Goularte, Portuguese.
(17) V. dos P.O. Gonsalves, Portuguese.
(18) E. M. Guterr□i, Portuguese.
(19) A. Mitchell Grant, Russian (English Parentage).
(20) B. Rapidoff, Russian.
(21) R. Perkins, American.

I have to report that with the exception of (2) J. Thomas
and (10) M. H. Iochvidoff, nothing is known to the detriment
of these gentlemen from a Police point of view whilst careful
enquiries show that they are individuals fit in all respects for
the type of work undertaken by the S.M.P. (Specials).

John Thomas was appointed as constable No. 18 in the
Shanghai Municipal Police on February 21, 1927, his services
with the Council terminating on December 11, 1929, when he
was dismissed for gross misconduct. His conduct during his
period of service, according to official records, was
"indifferent."
From December 1929 until June 30, 1930 Thomas was
unemployed, after which he worked on the staff of Mr. B.
Lennox-Simpson at Tientsin on the seizure by politico-military
force of the Tientsin Customs. He held this position until
October 1930, when with the death of Mr. Lennox-Simpson, his
organization was disbanded.
Thomas remained unemployed from that time until February
1931 when he obtained a position locally with Messrs. Andersen,
Meyer & Co. as a refrigerator salesman on a commission basis.
This job Thomas held until June 1931 when he resigned voluntarily,
after which he was again out of work until October 1931, when
he joined the National Flood Relief Commission and took charge
of all commissary work in Kiangse and parts of Anhwei and
Hupeh, with headquarters at Kiukiang, Kiangse. He was responsible
for the disbursing of funds amounting to Mex.$140,000.00 and
grain valued at Mex.$1,500,000.00. He left this billet in
July 1932 on the completion of work in the areas stated above.
From July 1932 he was again unemployed for a long period and in
late December 1932 and early January 1933 he submitted
applications for a position as Assistant-Warder on the S.M.C.
Gaol Staff. His applications, however, were not approved
and the following letter was addressed to Thomas on January 23,
1933, by the Extra Commissioner of Police:-

约翰·托马斯（John Thomas）于1927年2月21日被任命为上海公共租界工部局警务处第18号巡捕，其服务于1929年12月11日终止，当时他因严重行为不端被开除。根据官方记录，他在服役期间的表现“平平”。
从1929年12月至1930年6月30日，托马斯处于失业状态，此后他在天津受雇于B. Lennox-Simpson先生麾下，参与以政治军事力量接管天津海关的行动。他一直担任该职务直至1930年10月，随着Lennox-Simpson先生去世，其组织解散。
此后托马斯一直失业，直到1931年2月，他在本地安得利洋行（Andersen, Meyer & Co.）获得一份按佣金计算的冰箱销售员职位。托马斯担任此职直至1931年6月自愿辞职，之后再次失业，直到1931年10月加入全国水灾救济委员会，负责江西及安徽、湖北部分地区的给养工作，总部设在江西九江。他负责发放金额达墨西哥银元140,000.00元的资金以及价值墨西哥银元1,500,000.00元的粮食。1932年7月，鉴于上述地区工作完成，他离开了该职位。
从1932年7月起，他又长期失业，并在1932年12月底和1933年1月初提交了申请，谋求工部局监狱职员中的助理狱警职位。然而，他的申请未获批准，警务处副总巡官于1933年1月23日向托马斯致函如下：

relative of A. A. Iochvidoff, proprietor of an establishment

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by J.B.K. S.

With reference to the attached application of
Frederick Charles Whiddett to join S.M.P. (Specials),
enquiries show that this individual is an unrecognised
British subject, 23 years of age. He was educated in
the St. Francis Xavier's College, No.24 Nanzing Road, which
he left about five years ago. Upon leaving the school he
worked for some time in a printing establishment and for
the past three years has been employed as a clerk with the
"China Theatres Limited", No.2 Park Road.

His father, a British subject, who died seven
years ago, worked for many years as a chief-steward on
various steamers of the P.& O. S.N. Co., as well as of the
shipping companies represented by Butterfield & Swire, and
was later employed as manager of the Grill Cafe, Broadway.
He was married to a Japanese woman. For some reason F.C.
Whiddett, their son, was not registered with the local
British Consulate-General.

F.C. Whiddett resides with his mother at No.84
MacGregor Road. He has a good reputation and nothing
detrimental is known by this office against him.

G. Tcheremshansky

Subject (in full) George K. Fowles alias Gomer Kireaf, applicant
to join S.M.P. (Specials).
Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by
With reference to the attached application of George
K. Fowles to join S.M.P. (Specials), enquiries show that this
individual's correct name is Gomer Kireaf. With permission
of his step father, Mr. J. Fowles, British, Collector of the
Revenue Department S.M.C., Kireaf prefers to be known under
the name of George K. Fowles, although he is registered with
the local Chinese Bureau of Public Safety under his proper
name.
Gomer Kireaf, Turkish, was born on December 26, 1914
at Peking. His father, who died at Harbin several years ago,
was a clerk by profession. In 1927 G. Kireaf arrived at
Shanghai from Harbin, together with his mother who, two years
later, married Mr. J. Fowles. In Shanghai he attended Public
School for Boys for 4 years. For the past one and half years
he was employed as an apprentice-mechanic in the workshops of
the China General Omnibus Co. Ltd., No.263 Connaught Road.
Kireaf's parents object to his joining S.M.P. (Specials),
as he is only 19 years of age, and is physically weak and short-
sighted. Kireaf states that the main reason for his application
to join Specials was his wish to play in the Police football team.
Kireaf resided with his parents at House 16, Lane 215,
Medhurst Road.
G. Tcheremshansky
D. S.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

关于所附乔治·K·福尔斯申请加入上海公共租界工部局警务处（特别队）一事，经查，此人的真名为戈默·基雷夫。在其继父、英籍人士、工部局税务局收款员 J·福尔斯先生的允许下，基雷夫更倾向于使用乔治·K·福尔斯这一名字，尽管他在当地中国公安局是以其真名注册的。

戈默·基雷夫，土耳其人，1914年12月26日出生于北京。其父数年前死于哈尔滨，生前职业为职员。1927年，G·基雷夫与其母从哈尔滨抵达上海，其母于两年后嫁给了 J·福尔斯先生。在上海，他就读于公立男校4年。在过去的一年半里，他在康纳路263号中国公共汽车股份有限公司的车间担任学徒技工。

基雷夫的父母反对他加入上海公共租界工部局警务处（特别队），因为他年仅19岁，且身体虚弱、患有近视。基雷夫称，他申请加入特别队的主要原因是希望参加警队足球队。

基雷夫与其父母居住在麦赫斯特路215弄16号。

G·切列姆尚斯基

March 15th. 37.
9. 30.

10 a.m. to 1.15 p.m. Italian Consular Court.

Further to diary 8, the copy of the S.S.D.Court
judgment was received and handed over to Judge Rapex,
Italian Consular Judge on 9/3/37.

The accused Francesco Contini was removed from
Ward Road Gaol on 15/3/37 and taken to the Italian
Consular Court for trial at 10.30 a.m.

After the evidence of the witnesses in this case
the following decision was given:-

" The Court finds the accused, Francesco Contini
guilty of having concurred in the crime of Fraud,
aggravated by the number of persons, we hereby sentence
him to eight months imprisonment and fined Six hundred
and sixty-six lire, with costs and damages.

During the above period he is to be deported to
Italy."

Arrangements have been made for the collection
of the S.M.P.(S) uniform of Contini at 4 p.m. 16/3/37
after which same will be handed over to the Special
Police Headquarters, together with the pistol and
ammunition already detained at Bubbling Well Station.

Contini was escorted to Ward Road Gaol by P.S.
Miller at 4.30 p.m. 15/3/37.

Copy attached for information of D.G.(Specials).

（印：S. M. P. / Boarding House Section. / Received / 16/3/37. / Mr. locati）

9. 30.

上午10时至下午1时15分 意大利领事法庭。

继日记第8条之后，收到上海特区法院判决书副本，并于1937年3月9日移交给意大利领事法官 Rapex 法官。

被告弗朗切斯科·孔蒂尼于1937年3月15日从提篮桥监狱提出，并于上午10时30分带至意大利领事法庭受审。

在本案证人作证后，作出如下判决：

“本庭认定被告弗朗切斯科·孔蒂尼犯有参与诈骗罪，因涉及人数众多而加重情节，特此判处其有期徒刑八个月，并处罚金六百六十六里拉，以及诉讼费和损害赔偿金。

在上述期间，将其驱逐出境至意大利。”

已安排于1937年3月16日下午4时收回孔蒂尼的上海公共租界工部局警务处（特别队）制服，随后将连同已在静安寺巡捕房扣押的手枪和弹药一并移交特别警察总部。

孔蒂尼于1937年3月15日下午4时30分由警士米勒（Miller）押送回提篮桥监狱。

Subject Rolf Audouard, applicant to join the S.M.P. (Specials).

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by D. S. J. Boyne

Enquiries show that Rolf Audouard is a German citizen,
30 years of age, holding a German passport No. 170, issued
on June 11, 1934, by the German Consulate-General, Shanghai
His home address is No. 19 Rustplatz, Hanover. Audouard
is employed with Dodge & Seymour (China), Ltd., No. 51
Canton Road, room 200, tel. 15495, and is also a representative
of Marks & Co. (General Importers).
In 1931 Audouard married one Merriam Griffin, American
(File D.6394), journalist by occupation, who at that time
was connected with the editorial staff of the North China
Daily News. Audouard, together with his wife, visited
Germany in 1934 and returned back to Shanghai via Siberia
and Dairen on December 5, 1934, by s.s. "Hoten Maru."
Mrs. Audouard died on December 28, 1934, as a result of
overdose of veronal taken as a sleeping potion.
Audouard is well known for his radical and pro-Soviet
sympathies. He and his late wife were associated with
Edmond Egon Kish (File D. 2919), Czechoslovakian Jew,
novelist by occupation, during Kish's visit to Shanghai in
1932. E. E. Kish is a well known member of the Anti-
Imperialist League and the Struggle Committee of Artist and
Writers (an organisation sponsored by the Third International).
Audouard is reported to be a heavy drinker and a man
of extravagant tastes.
Audouard is a member of the German A.D.C. He resides
at No. 153 Route de Say Zoong, Tel. 75429.

g. tcheremshansky
D. S.

D.C. (Special Br.)

现年30岁，持有德国护照第170号，该护照于
1934年6月11日由德国驻上海总领事馆签发。
其家庭住址为汉诺威 Rustplatz 19号。奥杜阿尔
受雇于道奇与西摩（中国）有限公司（Dodge & Seymour (China), Ltd.），地址为广东路51号200室，电话15495，同时也是

1931年，奥杜阿尔与梅里亚姆·格里芬（Merriam Griffin，美国人，

1934年访问德国，并于1934年12月5日经西伯利亚

奥杜阿尔夫人于1934年12月28日因服用过量
作为安眠药的维罗那（veronal）而死亡。
奥杜阿尔以其激进及亲苏倾向而闻名。

艺术家作家斗争委员会（由第三国际赞助的组织）的知名成员。
据报，奥杜阿尔酗酒且生活奢靡。
奥杜阿尔是德国 A.D.C. 的成员。他居住于
赛宗路（Route de Say Zoong）153号，电话75429。

Made by D.S. Poole. Forwarded by D.S.J. Byrne.

With reference to the attached applications of four
foreigners and one Chinese for enlistment in the Shanghai
Municipal Police (Specials) whose names are numerated below.
I have to report that there is nothing in police records
detrimental to the character of any of them.
1. Frederick William Brandt (British).
2. F.A. Sangster (British Eurasian).
3. Richard Bayfield Foster-Kemp (British).
4. Joseph Charles Leon (Chinese. (British protected?)
5. Antonio Maria Fonseca (Portuguese).

The fourth mentioned person J.C. Leon states in his
application form that he is a Chinese with British nationality.
He was born in Hongkong of British parentage and came to
Shanghai at the age of 4. He has however never registered
with the H.B.M. Consulate since his arrival and unless he can
produce a Hongkong birth certificate cannot be considered as a
British subject. Mr. North of H.B.M. Consulate Passport
Office has stated that he will interview this gentleman with
a view to obtaining full particulars of his birth and national
status, and will in turn inform the undersigned.

D. S.

Subject R.O. Kopelman, applicant to join S.M.P. (Specials)

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky. Forwarded by D S J Cooper

With reference to the attached Recruiting Form of
R. Kopelman, enquiries made show that Rudolph Osipovitch Kopelman
is a Russian Jew, born on December 19, 1906, at Shanghai. His
father is a retired merchant who resides at Shanghai. R. Kopelman
registered with the local Bureau of Public Safety as a Russian
Emigrant, under No.12726. He left Shanghai for Russia in
his early childhood together with his parents. In 1919 after
the Russian Revolution R. Kopelman left Sebastopol, Russia,
during the evacuation of the "White" Russians and proceeded to
England via Constantinople. In England he received his education
at Clifton College and subsequently studied for two years at
Cambridge University. In 1925 he left for France and remained
there until 1928 when he left for Germany. In Hamburg, Germany,
he was employed with B.A. Shoultz & Co. during 1929-1930. In
1931 Kopelman arrived at Hongkong as a representative of certain
firms and remained there until June 1933 when he left for Shanghai.
At Shanghai R. Kopelman, in August 1933, joined as a
partner a known local firm, S.J. Levy & Co., No.115 Kiukiang
Road (Investment Brokers & Brokers in Securities), where he is
working at present.
R. Kopelman resides at No.142 Museum Road, Flat 48.
Nothing detrimental is known by this office against the applicant.

With reference to the attached application of C. L.
Bogorodsky for enlistment in the S.M.P. (Specials), enquiries
elicit the following:-
Constantin Leonidovitch Bogorodsky, Russian, born on
21.5.1917 at Petrograd. His father, L.I. Bogorodsky
(File D.6554), who formerly was an official of the Russian
Imperial Customs, arrived in Manchuria following the outbreak
of the revolution in Russia in 1917. However, in 1923 he
returned to the U.S.S.R. In this connection it was rumoured
that he was obliged to do so, as he had been connected with
a Chinese General who, being supported by the Soviet, started
a rebellion in the region of Pogranichnaia Station of the
Chinese Eastern Railway in 1923, but was defeated and fled
to the U.S.S.R. It is also said that, while in the U.S.S.R.,
L.I. Bogorodsky was employed in the Vladivostok office of
the Finance Department of the Soviet Government. In 1930
he appeared in Shanghai. He stated that he had escaped
from the U.S.S.R.
The applicant arrived in Shanghai from Vladivostok in
1926, together with his mother, having left the U.S.S.R. with
permission of the Government. He received his education in
the St. Joan of Arc's College, No. 18 Route Doumer, and
subsequently in the College Municipal Francais and Thomas
Hanbury School. He was member of the Cadet Company, S.V.C.,
of the latter school for one year.
Some time during the latter part of 1934 he received
employment as a supervisor of works with the Acme Engineering
Co., Ltd., 128 Museum Road. Two months later he left that
firm in order to join the Universal Engineering Co., No.209

to Christianity he has taken the name of Francis Luthur Mori.

the St. Xavier College, Nanking Road, where he studied over
6 years until 1929. Since September, 1929, he has been in the
employ of the Shanghai Water-works Co., 484 Kiangse Road.
There is nothing in the Municipal Police records to
the detriment of this person either criminally or politically.
However, his motorcycle license record card shows that he was
cautioned on September 22, 1931, and was fined one Yen on
November 11, 1931, for breach of Traffic Regulation Art. Five.

G. D. Jack, applicant for S.M.P. (Specials), has been
in China for over 30 years. Before the Great War, throughout
which he served with the British Forces, he was employed in
the Tientsin Land Investment Co. at Tientsin. After the War

is still engaged in this business.
During the 1925 trouble he served with the S.M.P.
(Specials) as a sergeant in 5th Division. Nothing in police
records detrimental to the character of G.D. Jack.

Subject S. Zaharoff: applicant for S.M.P. (Specials).

Made by D.S. Jones Forwarded by [Signature] S.I.

with reference to the attached application by Mr. S. Zaharoff
for the post of constable in the Shanghai Municipal Police
(Specials), I have to report that there is nothing to the
applicant's detriment in Police records.
Enquiries made reveal that the applicant, Sergey Vasilievitch
Zaharoff, was born at Harbin on October 20, 1910. Vasilie
Vasilievitch Zaharoff, his father, died in 1924. His mother,
who is still living, resides in Harbin.
Zaharoff states that for six years he attended the Commercial
School at Harbin and completed his studies on attaining the age
of 19 years. Shortly after leaving school he came to Shanghai.
Since his arrival here he has had several jobs of a temporary
nature. For a little more than a year he was employed by
Carl Crow Inc., 81 Jinkee Road, acting as outside-man in charge
of a gang of coolies. His services while engaged with this
firm were satisfactory. He resigned in order to better himself
towards the end of 1933. On July 10, 1934 Zaharoff applied
for the position of Police Watchman, but as there were no
vacancies at the time he was unsuccessful in securing the
appointment.
Shortly after arrival in Shanghai Zaharoff registered with
the Russian Emigrants Association. There appears to be no
connection between Sergey Vasilievitch Zaharoff and the Serge
Alexander Zaharoff mentioned in my previous report as having
served a sentence of 50 days imprisonment for larceny.
Zaharoff has been in his present place of employment -
Arcwelding and Diecasting Works Ltd., 781 Wuting Road - for the
past fourteen months.

Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch)

关于附上的 S. 扎哈罗夫先生申请担任上海公共租界工部局警务处（特别队）巡捕一职的申请书，兹报告如下：警方记录中无任何不利于该申请人之记载。

经查，申请人谢尔盖·瓦西里耶维奇·扎哈罗夫（Sergey Vasilievitch Zaharoff）于1910年10月20日出生于哈尔滨。其父瓦西里·瓦西里耶维奇·扎哈罗夫（Vasilie Vasilievitch Zaharoff）于1924年去世。其母尚在世，居住于哈尔滨。

扎哈罗夫称，他在哈尔滨商业学校就读六年，年满19岁时完成学业。离校后不久即来到上海。抵沪以来，他曾从事数份临时性工作。他在金尼路81号卡尔·克劳公司（Carl Crow Inc.）任职一年多，担任负责管理一群苦力的外勤人员。在该公司任职期间，其表现令人满意。他于1933年底辞职以谋求更好发展。1934年7月10日，扎哈罗夫申请警署更夫职位，但因当时无空缺而未获录用。

扎哈罗夫抵沪后不久即在俄国侨民协会登记。谢尔盖·瓦西里耶维奇·扎哈罗夫与我此前报告中提到的因盗窃罪被判监禁50天的谢尔盖·亚历山大·扎哈罗夫（Serge Alexander Zaharoff）之间似乎并无关联。

扎哈罗夫目前在武定路781号电弧焊接与压铸有限公司（Arcwelding and Diecasting Works Ltd.）任职，已过去十四个月。

Made by...D.S. Jones................Forwarded by..DB Ross D.
With reference to the attached application by Mr. George
Oswald Davies for a position as constable in the Shanghai
Municipal Police (Specials), I have to report that there is
nothing to the detriment of the applicant in Police records.
Applicant attended St. Xavier's College, No.281 Nanzing
Road, from September, 1921 to February, 1928 and left with
a good record. Shortly after leaving school he went to
Tientsin and from June 1929 to July 1930 was employed by the
Texas Company, Tientsin. While with this company his
services were very satisfactory, and it was because of a
reduction in staff due to lack of business that he was
discharged.
From May 1931 to November 1931 Davies was in the employ
of Colgate-Palmolive-Beet Co., 3 Canton Road. He resigned
his position with this firm in order to better himself.
Davies left Shanghai for Tientsin towards the end of
1931 and in April 1932 he obtained a position as accountant
with Fox Film Federal Inc., U.S.A., Tientsin Branch. He
remained there until May 1933 when he resigned. Late in
1934 he returned to Shanghai. Davies has been with the
Universal Picture Corporation, 623 Szechuen Road, the firm
which now employs him, since March 15, 1935.
The applicant has good reference from each of the
firms for which he previously worked.

1. George Frederichs DAMMERS, Netherlands subject, was
born on November 8, 1888, at Amsterdam and has normal school
education. Prior to his arrival in Shanghai in September,
1934 he resided for several years in the Netherlands Indies.
In Shanghai he was employed for some time first with Milling-
ton, Ltd., 668 Szechuen Road, and then with Frisland China
Trading Co., 160 Avenue Edward VII. At present he is employed
with Union Brewery Ltd., No. 220 Szechuen Road, Wayfoong House.
Dammers is registered with the local Netherlands Consulate-
General. He resides at No. 764/12 Rue Bourgeat (Tel. 75632)
with his wife and daughter.

2. Helmut Frantz Leonhardt BOMBACH, German, was born
on 20.2.1904. He received his education in a normal school
in Germany. From 1926 he has been employed with Fuhrmeister
& Co., No. 66 Museum Road, a well known local German firm.
From July 6, 1933 until February 15, 1936, the applicant served
in the Transport Company, S.V.C., in which he was a sergeant.
He resigned at his own request. His present address is
House 2, No. 355 Medhurst Road (Medhurst Court).

3. Leonid Moiseyevitch BUYANOVER, Russian, was born

Subject (in full) I.T. Illinsky, member of S.M.P. (Specials).
Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by J. Boyne O.I.I
With reference to the attached enquiry regarding the
conduct of I.T. Illinsky while a member of the S.V.C., I
have to state that it has been ascertained that during the
period in which he served in the 3rd Russian (Volunteer)
Company, Illinsky did not regularly attend his drills and
that when he resigned he was not prompt in handing in his
uniform, though the uniform was eventually returned.
Apart from this there is nothing detrimental concerning
Illinsky in the records of the S.V.C. His present place
of employment is the Shanghai Express Co., 150 Boone Road,
and his address is at House 25, No.159 Avenue Haig.

W.P. Mc Allan, applicant to join S.M.P. (Specials).

D.P.S. Henchman

William Primrose Mc Allan was born in 1899
at "Primrose Bank", Bonhill Road, Dumbarton, Scotland.
He attended the Dumbarton Academy from the age of 5
until he was 14. On leaving school he entered the
legal firm of Mc Arthur, Brown and Robinson in Dumbarton
but left after a few months and went to sea in a Henderson
line ship from Glasgow. During the war, still with the
same shipping company, he served in the Mercantile Fleet
Auxiliaries, and at the end of the War, in 1918, he left
Henderson's to sit for his 2nd mate's ticket. Having
obtained his ticket he sailed with the "Clan" line until
1919 when he left to sit for his 1st mate's ticket and then
rejoined Henderson's, employment with which firm he terminated
at his own request in 1921. In 1921 he obtained an employ-
ment with the Indo China Steamship Co. and sailed from
Glasgow in one of their ships, the "Pausang", for the
China coast where he remained until late in 1923. In 1924
Mc Allan left the sea for good and found employment with
the British Cigarette Co., Thorburn Road, which firm he left,
at his own request, in 1925 and joined the Shanghai Hongkew
Wharf to where he is now employed in their Pootung office.
From 1925 to 1927 Mc Allan served in the Scottish
Company of the S.V.C. and resigned owing to his being moved
to Pootung.
Nothing detrimental to Mc Allan's character is
known by this office.

D.C. (Special Branch)                                      D. P. S.

W.P. Mc Allan，申请加入工部局警务处（特别队）。

D.P.S. Henchman

William Primrose Mc Allan 于1899年出生在苏格兰邓巴顿邦希尔路的“Primrose Bank”。他从5岁到14岁就读于邓巴顿学院。离校后，他进入邓巴顿的 Mc Arthur, Brown and Robinson 律师事务所，但几个月后便离开，从格拉斯哥登上亨德森轮船公司（Henderson line）的船只出海。战争期间，他仍在同一家航运公司，在商业舰队辅助部队服役，战争结束后的1918年，他离开亨德森公司以考取二副证书。获得证书后，他在“Clan”轮船公司航行至1919年，随后离职去考取大副证书，之后重新加入亨德森公司，并于1921年自行请求终止了在该公司的雇佣关系。1921年，他在印度支那轮船公司（Indo China Steamship Co.）找到工作，并乘坐该公司的“Pausang”号船从格拉斯哥启航前往中国沿海，在那里一直待到1923年底。1924年，Mc Allan 彻底离开航海业，在索伯恩路的英国卷烟公司（British Cigarette Co.）找到工作，他于1925年自行请求离开该公司，加入上海虹口码头，目前受雇于该公司的浦东办事处。
1925年至1927年，Mc Allan 在万国商团苏格兰连服役，因被调往浦东而辞职。
本处未掌握任何对 Mc Allan 品行不利的情况。

副总监（特务科）                                      D. P. S.

Section 2, Special Branch___
December 14, 35.

I.T. Illinsky, applicant to join S.M.P. (Specials).

Inokenty Tihonovitch Illinsky, Russian born on
January 28, 1905 at Pogranichania Station, Central Eastern
Railway. He was educated in Nikolsk-Ussuriysk Gymnasium
graduating in 1921. He left for China in 1922 after the
defeat of the White Russian Army and proceeded to Pogranichnaia
where his father was a Minister of the Russian Orthodox Church.
A few months later he left for Harbin where he studied at
the Russian-Chinese Polytechnic (High School). In 1925
Illinsky arrived in Shanghai and for about 6 years after his
arrival he was employed as private tutor teaching the Russian
language. From 1928 to 1929 Illinsky received employed with
the Shanghai Water Works Company. After one year he left
this company at his own wish and joined the Foreign Y.M.C.A.,
150 Bubbling Well Road, as a building engineer. In 1930 he
left this service at his own request with a good testimonial
and received employment with Philips China Company, 133
Szechuen Road (Lamps, Radio, etc.) as a salesman engineer,
where he served from May 1 to June 15, 1931. He left this
firm with a good-service certificate and joined the Texas
Company (China) Ltd., 12 The Bund, as a salesman. He left this
employment in August 1934 and later established his own business
in partnership with one T. Banner (British) under the name of
Brown, Hill & Co., 24 The Bund. This Company is dealing with
motor car oil, grease, etc.

Illinsky was member of the Russian Volunteer Company
from 1927 to 1930 and resigned at his own request; he served
later with S.M.P. (Specials) from 1931 to 1932.

Illinsky resides at No.159/25 Avenue Haig. He is
registered with Russian Emigrants Committee.

特务科第二股___
1935年12月14日。

I.T. Illinsky，申请加入工部局警务处（特别队）。

Inokenty Tihonovitch Illinsky，俄国人，1905年1月28日出生于中东铁路边境站（Pogranichania Station）。他在乌苏里斯克尼古拉耶夫斯克中学（Nikolsk-Ussuriysk Gymnasium）接受教育，1921年毕业。1922年白俄军队战败后，他前往中国，到达边境站（Pogranichnaia），他的父亲在那里担任东正教牧师。几个月后，他前往哈尔滨，在俄华理工中学（Russian-Chinese Polytechnic (High School)）学习。1925年，Illinsky 抵达上海，在抵达后的约6年里，他受雇担任私人教师，教授俄语。1928年至1929年，Illinsky 受雇于上海自来水公司。一年后，他自愿离开该公司，加入位于静安寺路150号的外国青年会（Foreign Y.M.C.A.），担任建筑工程师。1930年，他持良好的推荐信自愿离职，并在四川路133号的飞利浦中国公司（Philips China Company）（经营电灯、收音机等）受雇担任销售工程师，任职时间为1931年5月1日至6月15日。他持服务证明书离开该公司，加入位于外滩12号的德士古公司（中国）有限公司（Texas Company (China) Ltd.），担任销售员。他于1934年8月离开该职位，后来与一名英国人 T. Banner 合伙创办了自己的企业，名为 Brown, Hill & Co.，地址在外滩24号。该公司经营汽车机油、润滑脂等。

Illinsky 于1927年至1930年是俄国志愿连的成员，并自行请求辞职；他后来于1931年至1932年在工部局警务处（特别队）服役。

Illinsky 居住在海格路159/25号。他在俄国侨民委员会注册。

Section 2, Special Branch.xxxxx
December 13, 35.

Mihail Ivanovitch Grigorieff, applicant to join S.M.P.
(Specials).

Mihail Ivanovitch Grigorieff was born 27th December
1916 at Station Raevka, Ufa Province. He arrived in
China together with his parents after the defeat of the
White Russian Army in 1920, and resided over one year at
Changchun and subsequently for two years at Mukien. In
1925 he arrived at Shanghai from Manchuria. He was
educated at the 1st Russian School, Yulin Road, and subsequentl
in College Municipal Francais, No. 11 Route Vallon. In
1931 Grigorieff received employment as a newspaper delivery
man. He left this service after two months and for about
six months was unemployed. Later he was employed for 3
months at the Blue Cross (Veterinary) Hospital, No. 170
Edinburgh Road. He left this service owing to a disagreement
with Mr. M. W. Lehmann alias Lugowoy (S.B. Files D.2401 and
D.1780), the owner of the hospital, and again was unemployed
for a period of 5-6 months. He next obtained employment
as a shop assistant in a provision store at No. 52 Rue
Delfus; Grigorieff left this employment after 6 months and
on July 1933 joined Keylock & Pratt (Veterinary surgeons),
381 Liangchow Road, where he is still working.

Grigorieff's late father was a specialist in soap
manufacture and a mason by occupation.

He resides with his mother and two brothers at 210
Rue Wantz. His brother Nikolay Ivanovitch Grigorieff is a
member of the 3rd Company of the Russian Regiment. M.I.
Grigorieff is registered with the Russian Emigrants Committee.
Nothing detrimental to the character of the applicant is
known by this department.

特务科第二股.xxxxx
1935年12月13日。

Mihail Ivanovitch Grigorieff，申请加入工部局警务处（特别队）。

Mihail Ivanovitch Grigorieff 于1916年12月27日出生在乌法省的 Raevka 车站。1920年白俄军队战败后，他与父母一同来到中国，在长春居住了一年多，随后在奉天（Mukien）居住了两年。1925年，他从满洲抵达上海。他在榆林路的第一俄国学校接受教育，随后在万隆路11号的市立法文中学（College Municipal Francais）就读。1931年，Grigorieff 受雇担任送报员。两个月后他离开了这份工作，失业了约六个月。后来，他在爱丁堡路170号的蓝十字（兽医）医院工作了3个月。由于与医院老板 M. W. Lehmann 先生（又名 Lugowoy，特务科档案 D.2401 和 D.1780）发生争执，他离开了这份工作，再次失业5-6个月。随后，他在德尔福斯路52号的一家食品店受雇担任店员；Grigorieff 在这份工作6个月后离职，并于1933年7月加入位于凉州路381号的 Keylock & Pratt（兽医外科医生诊所），至今仍在那里工作。

Grigorieff 已故的父亲是肥皂制造专家，职业为泥瓦匠。

他与母亲及两个兄弟居住在万茨路210号。他的兄弟 Nikolay Ivanovitch Grigorieff 是俄国团第三连的成员。M.I. Grigorieff 已在俄国侨民委员会注册。
本部门未掌握对该申请人品行不利的情况。

Section 2, Special Br. xxxxx
November 29, 35.

S. F. soldatenkoff, applicant to join S.M.P. (Specials).

Sergius Fedorovitch Soldatenkoff, Russian, was born in
1901 in Kaluga Province and spent his early childhood in
Chita, Transbaikal Province, where his father was employed in
the Siberian Railway. He was educated at Alexandrovsky
Normal School at Chita, and after having graduated he was
employed for some time at the Chernovskaia Railway Station as
a clerk. In 1918 he joined the Chita Military School
organized by Ataman Semenoff and in 1920 he received the rank
of sub-lieutenant of Engineers. He took part in the Civil
War in Transbaikal and Maritime Province and served in a
number of different detachments. In 1922, after the defeat
of the White Army, he went to Kirin Province and shortly after,
he proceeded to Harbin where he was engaged by casual work until
1926. Late in 1926 he arrived in Shanghai and was employed in
the Christian Book Room No. 3 Quinsan Garden for 6 months, after
leaving this employment he worked for about 5 months with the
Lucerne Dairy Farm, No.381 Great Western Road. From 7th Sept.
1928 he was employed as an engineer with the Foreign Y.M.C.A.
No.150 B'well Road but left in May 1933 when a reduction of
staff took place. In 1933 Soldatenkoff left Shanghai for Tien-
tsin and was employed there for a few months with Reuters Limited
as an engineer but again had to leave his employment owing to
a reduction of staff. In 1934 Soldatenkoff received employment
with the American Presbetarian Missions in Anhwei where he was
engaged in carrying out repairs at a Gas and Electric Station.
He remained there for 5 months and on May 1935 he returned to
Shanghai. Since that time he has been un-employed . Soldatenkoff
is married and had two children, one daughter aged 9 and a son
aged 7. He resides at No.66/28 Route Lorton.

1935年11月29日。

S. F. soldatenkoff，申请加入工部局警务处（特别队）。

Sergius Fedorovitch Soldatenkoff，俄国人，1901年出生于卡卢加省，童年早期在外贝加尔省的赤塔度过，他的父亲当时在西伯利亚铁路工作。他在赤塔的亚历山德罗夫师范学校（Alexandrovsky Normal School）接受教育，毕业后曾在切尔诺夫斯卡亚火车站（Chernovskaia Railway Station）担任职员一段时间。1918年，他加入了由谢苗诺夫阿塔曼（Ataman Semenoff）组织的赤塔军事学校，1920年获得工兵少尉军衔。他参加了外贝加尔和滨海省内战，并在多个不同分队服役。1922年白军战败后，他前往吉林省，不久后前往哈尔滨，在那里从事临时工作直到1926年。1926年底，他抵达上海，在昆山路花园3号的基督教书室（Christian Book Room）工作了6个月，离开这份工作后，他在大西路381号的卢塞恩奶牛场（Lucerne Dairy Farm）工作了约5个月。从1928年9月7日起，他在静安寺路150号的外国青年会（Foreign Y.M.C.A.）担任工程师，但在1933年5月因裁员而离职。1933年，Soldatenkoff 离开上海前往天津，在那里受雇于路透社有限公司（Reuters Limited）担任工程师数月，但因裁员不得不再次离职。1934年，Soldatenkoff 在安徽的美国长老会传教团（American Presbetarian Missions）找到工作，负责燃气和电站的维修工作。他在那里待了5个月，于1935年5月返回上海。自那时起，他一直处于失业状态。Soldatenkoff 已婚，育有两个孩子，一个9岁的女儿和一个7岁的儿子。他居住在劳顿路66/28号。

December 3, 35.

V.N. Shteher applicant to join S.M.P. (Specials).

D.P.S. Henchman

Vsevolod Nikolaevitch Shtener, Russian born on
March 16, 1910 at Petrograd, arrived at Harbin in 1920 with
his parents after the defeat of the White Russian Army. He
was educated at Lomonossoff's Gymnasium at Harbin and
graduated in 1927. Later he served for a year as armed
watchman at the National City Bank of New York at Harbin
and subsequently was employed with this Bank as a clerk until 19
1931 when he was discharged owing to reduction of staff.
On September 20, 1931 he arrived at Shanghai from Harbin
and shortly after his arrival he received a position with
Palmer & Turner, Property Office, No.17 Canton Road, where
he is still employed. He resides at Passage 51 House 12
Route de Grouchy with his parents. His father, previous
to the Russian Revolution, was an official in the Ministry
of Home Affairs and during the Civil War in Siberia he served
in the Military Administrative Office of Admiral Kolchak,
Dictator of Siberia.

Shteher is registered with the Soro (Council
of the Russian United Organization at Shanghai).
From January 5, 1932 until May 1935 Shteher served in the
Light Battery S.V.C.. He resigned on his own request.
S.I. A.Algazin and F.S. A.Algazin of S.M.P. are his cousins.

Nothing detrimental known by this office against
the applicant.

)
D. P. S.

弗谢沃洛德·尼古拉耶维奇·什特内尔（Vsevolod Nikolaevitch Shtener），俄罗斯人，1910年3月16日出生于彼得格勒。白俄军队战败后，他于1920年随父母抵达哈尔滨。他就读于哈尔滨罗蒙诺索夫中学（Lomonossoff's Gymnasium），并于1927年毕业。此后，他在哈尔滨纽约国家城市银行（National City Bank of New York）担任武装警卫一年，随后受雇于该行担任职员，直至1931年因裁员被解职。1931年9月20日，他从哈尔滨抵达上海，抵沪不久便在广东路17号帕默与特纳事务所（Palmer & Turner）产权部获得职位，至今仍在此任职。他与父母同住于格罗西路（Route de Grouchy）51弄12号。其父在俄国革命前曾任内政部官员，在西伯利亚内战期间，曾在西伯利亚独裁者高尔察克海军上将的军事行政办公室服役。

什特内尔已在上海俄罗斯联合组织理事会（SORO）注册。从1932年1月5日至1935年5月，什特内尔在上海义勇军（S.V.C.）轻炮连服役。他主动辞职。上海公共租界工部局警务处的 S.I. A.Algazin 和 F.S. A.Algazin 是他的表亲。

本局未发现对该申请人不利的记录。

)

V.A. Rybakoff, applicant to join S.M.P. (Specials).

D.S. Henchman

Vladimir Alexandrovitch Rybakoff, Russian
born on June 27, 1915 at Harbin. His father who is dead,
was an employee of the Chinese Eastern Railway. Rybakoff
was educated in the 1st Harbin Gymnasium and subsequently
at the French Municipal College, Shanghai. He arrived
in Shanghai in 1937, and soon after his arrival received
employment with the Russian newspaper Slovo as reporter
and clerk. He is still employed in this capacity.
Rybakoff joined "B" Company of S.V.C. in
1933 but after three months he resigned. He resides at
No.637 Avenue Joffre, house 5b a boarding house owned by
his mother. He is registered with the Russian Emigrants
Committee.
Nothing detrimental known by this office
against the applicant.

D. P. B.

弗拉基米尔·亚历山德罗维奇·雷巴科夫（Vladimir Alexandrovitch Rybakoff），俄罗斯人，1915年6月27日出生于哈尔滨。其父（已故）曾是中国中东铁路雇员。雷巴科夫就读于哈尔滨第一中学，随后就读于上海法公董局立学校（French Municipal College, Shanghai）。他于1937年抵达上海，抵沪不久便在俄文报纸《斯洛沃报》（Slovo）担任记者和职员。他目前仍以此身份受雇。雷巴科夫于1933年加入上海义勇军（S.V.C.）“B”连，但三个月后辞职。他居住在霞飞路637号5b室，该寄宿舍为其母所有。他已在俄罗斯侨民委员会注册。

Subject. L. C. TOURICK, applicant to join the S.M.P. (Specials).
Made by. D.S.I. Prokofiev Forwarded by. J. ...
Leonid Codratievitch TOURICK, Russian, was born on June 8,
1912 at Chita, Transbaikal province, Siberia. According to his
own statement he graduated from a secondary school in Habarovsk
in 1929 and subsequently attended a navy school (radio operators'
section) at Vladivostock for about one year, after which, in 1931,
he fled from the U.S.S.R. to China together with his father and
resided in Harbin until his departure for Shanghai some time
towards the end of 1932.
In Shanghai he worked casually as a radio mechanic until
March, 1934 when he joined the Radio Sales Corporation, 82
Nanking Road. He left this firm owing to a reduction in staff
and with a good testimonial and from January, 1936 worked with
the General Engineering & Construction Co., 505 Honan Road,
for about six months, after which he resigned. Mr. Marvromati,
manager of the firm, was confidentially interviewed regarding
the applicant's character. He states that he suggested to
Tourick to resign because the latter was inclined to drinking.
However, he gave him a good testimonial.
Upon leaving the General Engineering & Construction Co.,
Tourick has been without fixed employment.
He resides at No. 697 Avenue Joffre where he occupies room
No. 8.
When registering with the Russian Emigrants' Committee in
October, 1932, Tourick mentioned a local resident as a reference.
However, the latter states that he hardly has any knowledge of
the applicant.
Interviewed in connection with his application, Tourick
mentioned the names of another two local Russian residents who,
he stated, knew him well. Curiously enough, the two individuals

列昂尼德·科德拉季耶维奇·图里克（Leonid Codratievitch TOURICK），俄罗斯人，1912年6月8日出生于西伯利亚外贝加尔省赤塔。据其自述，他于1929年毕业于哈巴罗夫斯克的一所中学，随后在海参崴的海军学校（无线电操作员班）就读约一年，之后于1931年与其父一起从苏联逃往中国，并居住在哈尔滨，直到1932年底某时离开前往上海。

在上海，他零星从事无线电机械师工作，直到1934年3月加入南京路82号无线电销售公司（Radio Sales Corporation）。该公司因裁员而将其解雇，并出具了良好的推荐信。从1936年1月起，他在河南路505号通用工程建筑公司（General Engineering & Construction Co.）工作了约六个月，随后辞职。该公司经理 Marvromati 先生就申请人的品行接受了秘密问询。他表示，他建议图里克辞职，因为后者有饮酒倾向。不过，他还是给了图里克一份良好的推荐信。

离开通用工程建筑公司后，图里克一直无固定职业。
他居住在霞飞路697号，占用8号房间。
1932年10月在俄罗斯侨民委员会注册时，图里克提到一名当地居民作为推荐人。然而，后者表示他对申请人几乎一无所知。

Subject V.A. Slobodchikoff and P.N. Volk-Levonovitch, applicants to

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev Forwarded by J. Lyon E.J.

1) Vladimir Alexandrovitch SLOBODCHIKOFF, Russian, was
born on 30.9.1913 at Samara, Russia. It is reported that he
left Russia for China in 1919 together with his parents and
resided in Harbin where he graduated from a middle school and
subsequently studied at the Faculty of Law for about three
years. In September 1935 he came to Shanghai from Harbin and
worked with his father, a local legal practitioner with an
office at Apt. 5, No. 368 Rue Bourgeat, until April, 1936,
when he entered the Aurora University to continue his studies
of law.
His two brothers, L.A. Slobodchikoff, 26, and N. A. Slo-
bodchikoff, 25, have been employed with the French Police in
Shanghai since 1.9.34 and 1.12.1935 respectively.
The applicant resides at the above address together with
his father and brothers.

2) Peter Nikolaevitch VOLK-LEVONOVITCH, Russian, born
on 16.1.1908 in the Transbaikal province, Siberia. He is the
son of a railway employee who served with the Chinese Eastern
Railway in Harbin from 1917 to 1935 when he retired on pension.
Volk-Levonovitch senior, it is reported, applied for Soviet
passport in 1927, but upon his retirement from the C.E.R.
renounced his Soviet citizenship.
The applicant claims to have middle school education and
to hold a diploma of electrical and mechanical engineer issued
by the technical school attached to the Harbin Polytechnic
Institute. He first came to Shanghai in 1930 in quest of
employment. Being unsuccessful in this, he returned to Harbin
where, according to his own statement, he was employed with the
River Customs as a supervisor of technical works until 1934

1) 弗拉基米尔·亚历山德罗维奇·斯洛博奇科夫（Vladimir Alexandrovitch SLOBODCHIKOFF），俄罗斯人，1913年9月30日出生于俄罗斯萨马拉。据报道，他于1919年随父母离开俄罗斯前往中国，居住在哈尔滨，在那里从中学毕业，随后在法律系学习了约三年。1935年9月，他从哈尔滨来到上海，与其父一起工作，其父是一名当地法律从业者，办公室位于蒲石路368号5室，直到1936年4月，他进入震旦大学继续攻读法律。

2) 彼得·尼古拉耶维奇·沃尔克-列沃诺维奇（Peter Nikolaevitch VOLK-LEVONOVITCH），俄罗斯人，1908年1月16日出生于西伯利亚外贝加尔省。他是一名铁路员工的儿子，其父自1917年至1935年在哈尔滨的中国中东铁路服役，后退休领取养老金。据报道，老沃尔克-列沃诺维奇曾于1927年申请苏联护照，但在从中东铁路退休后放弃了苏联国籍。
申请人声称拥有中学学历，并持有哈尔滨工业大学附属技术学校颁发的机电工程师文凭。他于1930年首次来到上海寻找工作。由于未能成功，他返回哈尔滨，据其自述，他在那里受雇于江海关，担任工程技术监理，直到1934年

Subject N. I. Hasanoff (alias Hasanove), applicant to join the S.M.P.(Specials).

Made by D. S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by [签名]

The correct name of the applicant is Naum Ilich HASANOFF.
He is a Russian of Jewish origin, born on 7.9.1908 at Mglin
Mogileff province, West Russia, and is the son of a lumber
merchant (now dead) who resided in Harbin from 1908.
The applicant graduated from the Anders' Middle School in
Harbin in 1927 after which he was employed with J. A. Ravetta,
wine merchants, in that city for about two years. He arrived
in Shanghai in November, 1929, and soon afterwards obtained
employment as a salesman with Egal & Co., No. 25 Rue Chu Pao
San. He left this firm owing to some disagreement with the
proprietor and from 1930 has been employed with Frost, Bland
& Co., Ltd., No. 33 Szechuen Road, being at present in charge
of the Medical & Provision Department.
Hasanoff first registered with the Shanghai Public Safety
Bureau through the medium of the Council of United Russian
Organizations (SORO) on August 13, 1934, on the strength of visa
No. 2939 issued by the Kirin Bureau on 29.10.1929. He resides
at No. 162B Route Vallon with his mother and sister.
According to his own statement his elder brother left Harbin
for the U.S.S.R. in 1924 in order to continue his education.
Hasanoff's proposer to join the S.M.P. (Specials), one
D.B. Vilensky, a partner in the "Centurion Printing Co.", 61
Yangtsepoo Road, is known as a Soviet sympathiser and associate
of Soviet employees.

Tcheremshansky

Officer i/c Special Branch.

申请人的正确姓名是 Naum Ilich HASANOFF。他是犹太裔俄罗斯人，1908年9月7日出生于俄罗斯西部莫吉廖夫省姆格林，是一名木材商人（已故）的儿子，其父自1908年起居住在哈尔滨。
申请人于1927年毕业于哈尔滨安德斯中学（Anders' Middle School），随后在该市 J. A. Ravetta 葡萄酒商行受雇约两年。他于1929年11月抵达上海，不久后在朱葆三路25号 Egal & Co. 公司获得销售员职位。因与业主发生分歧，他离开了该公司，自1930年起受雇于四川路33号 Frost, Bland & Co., Ltd. 公司，目前负责医疗与食品部。
Hasanoff 最初于1934年8月13日通过俄罗斯联合组织理事会（SORO）向上海市公安局注册，依据的是吉林局于1929年10月29日签发的第2939号签证。他与母亲和姐姐同住于万隆路162B号。
据其自述，他的长兄于1924年离开哈尔滨前往苏联继续学业。
Hasanoff 加入上海公共租界工部局警务处（特别队）的提名人 D.B. Vilensky 是杨树浦路61号“百夫长印刷公司”（Centurion Printing Co.）的合伙人，此人被称为苏联同情者及苏联雇员的关联人士。

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by [签名]

Andrew Viacheslavovitch Repas, Russian, was born on
April 13, 1917 at Petrograd. His father, V. V. Repas, former
officer of the Russian Imperial Army, was a member of the
Shanghai Municipal Police from 1/7/21 to 30/11/28 and since
1929 has been employed with the Public Works Department, S.M.C.,
being at present an Inspector i/c of the Hongkew Park.

The applicant arrived in Shanghai from Vladivostock in
1919 with his parents. He was educated in the 1st Russian
School, No.27 Yulin Road, and subsequently in the St. Joan of
Arc's College, No.18 Route Doumer. Upon leaving the school
he has been working as a private teacher of languages. He was
formerly a member of the Russian Boyscouts Organization.

Repas resides with his parents at No.1 Kiangwan Road.
Nothing detrimental is known by this office against the
applicant.

Iosif Grigorievitch Patent, Russian of Jewish origin, was
born on 22/10/1911 at Irkutsk. His late father, a tailor by
occupation, arrived in Harbin from the U.S.S.R. in 1924 and was
employed with Bent Brothers (Furriers, Woollen Merchants & Out-
fitters) in that city until 1932 when he went to Shanghai and
was employed here first with U.J. Soskin, No.1141 Bubbling Well
Road and later with the Shanghai Branch of Bent Bros. & Co., No.755
61 Bubbling Well Road. The last named firm, the owner of which,
Y.M. Bent, was formerly a contractor of the Red Army, is reported
to be financed by the Moscow Narodny Bank.

The applicant was educated in a commercial school in Harbin.
In 1929 he left for Hongkong where for 8 months he attended the
St. Joseph's College. Upon returning to Harbin he was employed
as a clerk with Netherlands Insurance Co. He left this firm

Savely (Samuel) Iosifovitch Kozlinsky, Russian of Jewish
origin, was born on 15/5/1912 at Harbin. His late father, a
former employee of the Customs subsequently served as a porter
in the Hotel Modern in Harbin owned by one Kaspe.
After Kozlinsky's father left the Hotel Modern he resided
for some time in Shanghai where he owned an oil factory. In
1922 he left for Soviet Russia together with his family and
resided there in Chita and Vladivostok until 1925 when he
returned to Manchuria. Some time later he proceeded to
Australia where he remained about 18 months, after which he
returned to Harbin, where he served as a watchman with different
Soviet schools on the Chinese Eastern Railway until 1932 when
he returned to Shanghai.
The applicant attended a primary school in Vladivostok
from 1922-5. Upon his return in Harbin in 1925 he was employed
as a barber with the Hotel Modern and the "Elegant" Beauty
Parlour until June 1929, when he left for Shanghai. Here he
worked in the same capacity in various hairdressing salons.
For the past 3 months he has been employed in the hairdressing
salon at the Park Hotel.
According to applicant's own statement, his elder brother
M.I. Kozlinsky, 26, a chauffeur who resided in Shanghai in 1926-
1927 and then went to Harbin, had to leave Manchuria for the
U.S.S.R. during the Sino-Soviet conflict in 1929 on account
of his pro-soviet activities, and at present resides in Moscow
with his mother and two sisters.
Kozlinsky's cousin Mrs. L.A. Kniazev nee Kozlinsky, 27,
was brought before the old Mixed Court on 31/8/25 and 16/12/25
on charges of larceny and fraud. On both occasions she was

萨韦利（塞缪尔）·约瑟福维奇·科兹林斯基（Savely (Samuel) Iosifovitch Kozlinsky），犹太裔俄国人，1912年5月15日出生于哈尔滨。其已故父亲前为海关雇员，随后在哈尔滨由一名叫 Kaspe 的人拥有的现代饭店（Hotel Modern）担任搬运工。
科兹林斯基的父亲离开现代饭店后，曾在上海居住一段时间，在那里拥有一家油厂。1922年，他携家人前往苏维埃俄国，在赤塔和符拉迪沃斯托克居住至1925年，随后返回满洲。不久后他前往澳大利亚，在那里停留了约18个月，之后返回哈尔滨，在中东铁路的各所苏联学校担任看守，直至1932年返回上海。
申请人于1922年至1925年间在符拉迪沃斯托克的一所小学就读。1925年返回哈尔滨后，他在现代饭店和“Elegant”美容院担任理发师，直至1929年6月前往上海。在此处，他在各家理发店从事相同职业。过去3个月，他在国际饭店的理发店工作。
据申请人自称，其兄 M.I. Kozlinsky，26岁，是一名司机，1926-1927年间居住在上海，随后前往哈尔滨，因亲苏活动，在1929年中苏冲突期间不得不离开满洲前往苏联，目前与其母亲和两个姐妹居住在莫斯科。
科兹林斯基的表亲 L.A. Kniazev 夫人（娘家姓 Kozlinsky），27岁，曾于1925年8月31日和1925年12月16日因盗窃和欺诈指控被提审至老混合法庭。在这两次事件中，她均被

Subject Application of S.A. MAGNUSSEN, Danish, for enrolment in the
Shanghai Municipal Police (Specials).

Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by J. Coyne. C.S.I.

Born in Copenhagen, Denmark, some fifty years ago,
Svend Aage MAGNUSSEN is an old China hand, having resided in
this country for over thirty-one years, most of which has been
spent in Shanghai.

He applied to join the Police Department of the Shanghai
Municipal Council in August 1912, and when interviewed by the
then Captain-Superintendent of Police, carefully refrained
from informing his questioner that he had been previously
employed in the Health Department of the Council, a fact which
he also concealed when filling-in his application form.
Coupled with this, Magnussen gave the impression that he was
more or less of the "rolling stone" type, since he had already
left good employment locally in more than one instance.
Accordingly he was not recommended for a position in the
Police.

In February 1933 Magnussen was the defendant in a civil
suit brought before the Danish Consular Court by the Embassy
Hotel, whose representative filed a case of debt against him.
The case, which was eventually settled out of court, concerned
a sum of some $270.00.

Later in 1933, a number of prominent Danish residents
formed "Maelkeriet Dana" at 1182 Bubbling Well Road, a concern
for the disposal to the public of various Danish dairy products.
Magnussen obtained the post of manager and licensee of this
organisation. In May 1935 the Public Health Department
applied for a summons against Magnussen on the grounds that he
on May 10, 1935 had kept for sale margarine;-
(1) containing 0.25% boric acid preservative in excess of
the quantity allowed,

由 D.S. Pitts 呈报。经 J. Coyne. C.S.I. 转递。

Svend Aage MAGNUSSEN 约五十年前出生于丹麦哥本哈根，是一位老中国通，在华居住已超过三十一年，其中大部分时间在上海度过。

他于1912年8月申请加入上海公共租界工部局警务处，在接受时任警务处总监面试时，刻意未向询问者透露他此前曾在工部局卫生处任职的事实，在填写申请表时也隐瞒了这一情况。加之马格努森给人的印象是某种程度的“漂泊不定”类型，因为他已不止一次放弃了本地良好的工作职位。因此，他不获推荐担任警务处的职位。

1933年2月，马格努森成为丹麦领事法庭受理的一起民事诉讼的被告，原告为 Embassy Hotel（音译：大使馆饭店），其代表对他提起债务诉讼。该案最终庭外和解，涉及金额约为270.00元。

1933年晚些时候，一些知名的丹麦居民在南京西路1182号成立了“Maelkeriet Dana”，这是一家向公众销售各种丹麦乳制品的企业。马格努森获得了该机构经理及持牌人的职位。1935年5月，公共卫生处以马格努森于1935年5月10日持有待售的人造黄油为由，申请对其发出传票：
(1) 所含硼酸防腐剂超出允许量0.25%，

Michail Alekseyevich KORSHOONOFF, Russian, was born on
December 8, 1905 at Merv, Transcaspian Province. He studied
in the 1st Primary School in Samara and following the outbreak
of the revolution in Russia made his way to Vladivostok,
Maritime Province. In 1926 he fled from Vladivostok to Harbin
where he subsequently resided with his parents until 1929.
Towards the end of 1929 he came to Shanghai and for the
following year worked as a waiter in Jukoff's Restaurant,
Avenue Joffre.
From 1930 to 1932 he was employed as a Kennel man at the
Canidrome, 439 Avenue du Roi Albert.
In January 1933 he left for Canton, where he joined the
French Police in Shameen as a constable, in which capacity he
served until November 1935, when he resigned on his own accord.
Shortly afterwards he obtained a position of a radio
mechanic in the Radio Department of Messrs. "Farmer & Ferguson
Co.", General Merchants, Canton, where he was employed until
May 1936, when the above concern went into liquidation.
In June 1936 he returned to Shanghai and in November of the
same year obtained employment as a radio mechanic with the
American Radio Equipment Co., 55 Yuen Ming Yuen Road, where he
is still working.
M. Korshoonoff resides at 95 Joffre Terrace, French
Concession.

Eugeny Stanislavovich SITKO, Russian, was born on
November 21, 1912 at Tomsk, Siberia.
In 1929 he came to Harbin where he resided with his
parents and studied in the Pushkin Elementary School.

Michail Alekseyevich KORSHOONOFF，俄国人，1905年12月8日出生于外里海省梅尔夫。他在萨马拉第一小学就读，俄国革命爆发后，他前往滨海省符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）。1926年，他从符拉迪沃斯托克逃往哈尔滨，随后与父母一起居住至1929年。1929年底，他来到上海，并在接下来的一年里在霞飞路的 Jukoff's Restaurant（音译：朱科夫餐厅）担任侍者。
1930年至1932年，他在阿尔伯特王路439号的 Canidrome（跑狗厅）担任犬舍管理员。
1933年1月，他前往广州，在那里加入沙面法国警察部队担任警员，一直服务至1935年11月，当时他自愿辞职。
不久后，他在广州商人“Farmer & Ferguson Co.”（音译：法默与弗格森公司）的无线电部获得无线电技师的职位，他一直受雇于此，直到1936年5月上述公司清算。
1936年6月，他返回上海，并于同年11月在圆明园路55号的美国无线电设备公司获得无线电技师的职位，目前仍在此工作。
M. Korshoonoff 居住在法租界霞飞坊95号。

1. Henry Anthony Bartholomew PISANI, British subject by
birth, was born on May 4, 1893, at Constantinople. He is report-
ed to have seen active service during the Great War in the ranks
of Royal Field Artillery from the beginning of 1915 to the end of
1919. Prior to his coming to Shanghai from Harbin in August
1934 he resided for various periods at Constantinople, Athens,
Japan and Harbin. In Shanghai he has been employed as a care-
taker of the Washington Apartments, 303 Avenue Petain, for the
past two years and besides has been working as a clerk with
D. Wisner & Co., 185 Yuen Ming Yuen Road, since November, 1936. He
resides at Flat 14, 303 Avenue Petain.
Pisani holds British passport No. 110 issued on
July 14, 1933 at Harbin. He is registered at the local British
Consulate-General.

2. George Emile BRUDERER, Swiss, was born on May 16,
1904, at Appenzell (Wald), Switzerland. From his early boyhood
to the end of 1922 he resided in Vladivostok where he graduated
from school. He first arrived in Shanghai from Vladivostok in
1922 and shortly afterwards left for the United States where he
remained until 1924, after which he returned to Shanghai. In
1924-1926 he was without any fixed employment and occasionally
worked as an informer for the Municipal Police. From 1926 to
1929 he was employed with the Broadway Hotel in Tientsin. He
then returned to Shanghai and was subsequently employed first
with Singer Sewing Machine Co. for over two years, and later
with China Sewing Machine Co., 75 Rue du Consulat, for over one
year. Early in December 1936, in partnership with a Chinese
named Tai, he established his own business under the name of
SWISS-CHINA TRADING CO., (buying & selling liquidation cargo).

1. Henry Anthony Bartholomew PISANI，生来即为英国臣民，1893年5月4日出生于君士坦丁堡。据报他在第一次世界大战期间，从1915年初至1919年底，在皇家野战炮兵部队服役并参加实战。在1934年8月从哈尔滨来到上海之前，他曾在君士坦丁堡、雅典、日本和哈尔滨等地断续居住。在上海，过去两年他受雇担任霞飞路303号华盛顿公寓的管理员，此外，自1936年11月以来，他还在圆明园路185号的 D. Wisner & Co. 公司担任职员。他居住在霞飞路303号14室。
Pisani 持有1933年7月14日在哈尔滨签发的第110号英国护照。他已在当地英国总领事馆登记注册。

2. George Emile BRUDERER，瑞士人，1904年5月16日出生于瑞士阿彭策尔（Wald）。从幼年至1922年底，他居住在符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴），并在那里完成学业。他于1922年首次从符拉迪沃斯托克抵达上海，不久后前往美国，在那里停留至1924年，之后返回上海。1924年至1926年间，他没有固定职业，偶尔为工部局警务处充当线人。1926年至1929年，他在天津的百老汇大酒店受雇。随后他回到上海，先后受雇于胜家缝纫机公司（Singer Sewing Machine Co.）两年多，以及领事馆路75号的中国缝纫机公司（China Sewing Machine Co.）一年多。1936年12月初，他与一名姓戴的中国人合伙，以“瑞华贸易公司”（SWISS-CHINA TRADING CO.，买卖清算货物）的名义开设了自己的商行。

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by J. Payne D.I.I

Mohamad Hoossan Darwood, British subject (Burmese),
was born on July 15, 1903, at Rangoon. His late father was
a contractor by occupation. Applicant received his education
at a primary school at Burma. During the Great War he served
with Burma Bat. M. T. in Mesopotamia. In February, 1920,
he was discharged in Mandalay. From 1920 to 1922 he was
employed as a sailor on board various British ships and
visited Europe and America. In 1922 he was paid off in
Japan and shortly afterwards arrived in Shanghai. Here
Darwood was employed with the S.M.C. Fire Brigade, from
October, 1922 to June 30, 1936, when he was discharged owing
to a general reduction in the foreign staff with a good
service record. Subsequently, for about 5 months, he conducted
a food shop at Lane 211, House No. C.C.15 West Yuhang Road,
supplying customers with European, Malayan and Chinese food.
The venture proved to be a failure and at present he is
working as a broker and salesman on a commission basis.
He resides with his wife and child at House 24,
Lane 352 Miller Road.
Nothing detrimental is known by this office
against the applicant either politically or criminally.

Mohamad Hoossan Darwood，英国臣民（缅甸籍），1903年7月15日出生于仰光。其已故父亲职业为承包商。申请人在缅甸的一所小学接受教育。在第一次世界大战期间，他在美索不达米亚随缅甸营摩托运输队服役。1920年2月，他在曼德勒退役。从1920年到1922年，他在多艘英国船只上担任海员，并游历了欧洲和美洲。1922年他在日本结账离职，不久后抵达上海。在此，Darwood 于1922年10月至1936年6月30日期间受雇于工部局火政处，后因外籍员工普遍裁减而离职，服务记录良好。此后约5个月，他在西余杭路C.C.15号211弄经营一家食品店，向顾客供应欧式、马来式和中式食品。该尝试证明是失败的，目前他作为一名经纪人和销售员，按佣金制工作。

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by J Boyce D S I

Gaetano Russo, Italian subject, was born on January
8, 1906, at Naples. He served in the Italian Navy for 8
years and was Chief Petty Officer and Gunner Sergeant on the
Italian gunboat "Libia". He left the service with a good
record and from December 3, 1930 to March 31, 1933 was employed
as a Sub-Officer in the S.M.C.Fire Brigade. He resigned
from this service as he wished to marry and according to the
Fire Brigade regulations, an officer can marry only after
five years' service.

In 1934-5 he was connected with Pinto's Finance Bank,
46 Range Road, and subsequently with the Pinto Bank, 80
Nanking Road. He was on friendly terms with the proprietor
of these banks, a certain Vincenzo Pinto, Italian, a known
criminal, and for some time resided together with this
individual at No.216 Range Road. Pinto was prosecuted by
the Shanghai Municipal Police in June, 1935, for attempted
fraud. Russo's name was mentioned in connection with this
case. Although enquiries showed that Russo assisted Pinto
in falsifying accounts, there was not sufficient evidence to
prove a charge against him (Vide C.909/36, 1341/35 "A" Central,
September 16, 1935).

It is known that when a certain V. Tatistscheff was
giving evidence against Russo in connection with the case in
question, the latter was overheard by F.S. 223 Cook, on
escort duty, to say that he would kill Tatistscheff. In
this connection it must be noted that Russo has the reputation
of a hot tempered man who easily resorts to threats.

Upon the closure of the Pinto Bank, Russo was
unemployed for a period. From April, 1936, he has been employed

Gaetano Russo，意大利籍臣民，1906年1月8日出生于那不勒斯。他在意大利海军服役8年，曾在意大利炮舰“利比亚”号（Libia）上担任首席士官和炮术军士。他以良好的记录退役，并于1930年12月3日至1933年3月31日期间在工部局火政处担任下级官员。他辞职是因为希望结婚，而根据火政处规定，官员必须服役满五年后方可结婚。

1934-35年间，他与位于辣斐德路46号的平托金融银行（Pinto's Finance Bank）有关联，随后又与位于南京路80号的平托银行（Pinto Bank）有关联。他与这些银行的老板、意大利人 Vincenzo Pinto（一名已知的罪犯）关系友好，并曾与此人共同居住在辣斐德路216号一段时间。Pinto 于1935年6月因企图诈骗被上海公共租界工部局警务处起诉。Russo 的名字与此案有关。虽然调查显示 Russo 协助 Pinto 伪造账目，但没有足够的证据对他提出指控（参见 C.909/36, 1341/35 "A" Central, 1935年9月16日）。

据悉，当某位 V. Tatistscheff 就上述案件作证反对 Russo 时，负责护送任务的巡捕 Cook (F.S. 223) 听到 Russo 说他要杀死 Tatistscheff。对此必须指出的是，Russo 素有脾气暴躁、动辄威胁他人的名声。

平托银行关闭后，Russo 失业了一段时间。自1936年4月起，他受雇于

Kurt Maurice Steiner, is an unrecognised Czecho-Slovakien citizens. He was born on September 16, 1912, at Anaberg, Saxony, Germany. His late father was a merchant by occupation, and was the owner of the Steiner Import Co., 210 Kiukiang Road. Applicant was educated in a primary school in Czecho-Slovakia and subsequently studied in the Shanghai American School and in the Commercial Academy at Newchatel, Switzerland. He resided in Shanghai from 1923 to 1927 after which he left for Switzerland to continue his education. In 1930 he returned to Shanghai.

He was employed with the Banque Franco Chinoise pour le Commerce & l'Industrie, 1 French Bund, for some time. In 1931 he visited Italy and following his return to Shanghai was employed for a few months with the Steiner Import Co., owned by his mother and elder brother. Later he joined the New Zealand Perpetual Forests Ltd. 220 Szechuen Road and subsequently was transferred to the Nanking branch of that concern. At the same time he worked as an agent for the Office Appliance Co. Ltd., in Nanking. In 1934 he left for Europe where, it is reported he resided in Czecho-Slovakia, Austria and Spain for various periods. While in Europe, he joined the Bohler Bros. & Co. Ltd. and following his return to Shanghai in 1937 continued to work for the local branch of the firm, 107 Museum Road.

Steiner is married and resides at 1333 Avenue Joffre, Apt. "L". He holds a provisional Czecho-Slovakian passport issued by the Czecho-Slovakian Consulate at Milano, Italy.

Steiner served with the American Machine Gun Company, S.V.C., from 23.7.32 to 27.2.33 when he resigned on his own

Kurt Maurice Steiner，是一名未被承认的捷克斯洛伐克公民。他于1912年9月16日出生于德国萨克森州的阿纳贝格（Anaberg）。其已故父亲职业为商人，是九江路210号 Steiner 进口公司的所有者。申请人在捷克斯洛伐克的一所小学接受教育，随后在上海美国学校和瑞士纳沙泰尔商业学院学习。他于1923年至1927年居住在上海，之后前往瑞士继续学业。1930年他返回上海。

他曾在外滩1号的中法工商银行（Banque Franco Chinoise pour le Commerce & l'Industrie）工作了一段时间。1931年他访问了意大利，回到上海后，在他母亲和兄长拥有的 Steiner 进口公司工作了几个月。后来他加入位于四川路220号的新西兰永久森林有限公司（New Zealand Perpetual Forests Ltd.），随后被调往该公司的南京分行。同时，他在南京为办公设备有限公司（Office Appliance Co. Ltd.）担任代理。1934年他前往欧洲，据报道他在捷克斯洛伐克、奥地利和西班牙断续居住。在欧洲期间，他加入了 Bohler Bros. & Co. Ltd.，并在1937年返回上海后，继续在该公司的本地分支机构（博物馆路107号）工作。

With the exception of V. L. Ostapenko, P.R. Sokolov, K.M.
Steiner, and A. A. Savul nothing is known to the detriment of
the candidates mentioned in the attached list.
(1)V.L. Ostapenko was convicted on a charge of assault
(Cutting and Wounding) made by the French Police on May 3, 1931.
For this offence he was fined $3.00 suspended for 1 year. He
has been employed by the Shanghai Power Company, Riverside Station
since August 1928. His report card shows a long sick record
and he is reported to be a person of uncertain temper, and of
aggressive pugilistic temperament. There is no record of any
complaints in connection with his work however.
(2)P.R. Sokolov was charged with assault on one P. Sharoff
on May 27, 1931, and convicted by the Shanghai Special District
Court on June 8, 1931, when he was fined $50.00 or 25 days
imprisonment.
This assault was the immediate outcome of certain remarks
of an insulting nature which Sharoff is alleged to have made
with reference to the wife of Sokolov. Prior to the assault,
it was known that Sokoloff was the victim of a sharp business
deal engineered by Sharoff involving the sale of "Peter's
Beauty Parlour", 49 Nanking Road, when Sharoff is stated to have
failed to keep to an agreement not to open a similar business
locally under the same name. Sokoloff bears a good reputation
among the Russian community in Shanghai, while Sharoff is
regarded as a person of doubtful character. The opinion
of persons who are acquainted with the incidents mentioned, and
the characters of both men, is that Sharoff deserved the beating
at the hands of Sokoloff.

(2) P.R. Sokolov 被控于1931年5月27日袭击 P. Sharoff，并于1931年6月8日被上海特区地方法院定罪，当时他被罚款50.00元或监禁25天。

Made by D.S.Tcheremshansky Forwarded by C Crawford
Emmanuel Walter George Schweigert, Russian of German extraction, was born on August 1, 1908 at Habarovsk, Siberia. His late father was an officer of the Russian Imperial Army. In 1910 applicant arrived in Tsingtao from Russia together with his mother. In 1914 following the outbreak of the Great War, they proceeded to Shanghai where Schweigert entered the St. Francis Xavier's College, 281 Nanzing Road. Upon graduating in 1925, he left for Hankow, where from 1925 to 1932 he was employed with Thomson & Co. Chartered Accountants. From 1932 to 1936, he worked with the "Hankow Ice Works, Ltd". In 1936 Schweigert returned to Shanghai from Hankow and for a short period was employed temporary as a book-keeper with Haskins & Sells, 32 Szechuen Road, on leaving there was un-employed. He occassionally found part time work with Henry S. De Vault (Certified Public Accountant), 51 Canton Road. In May 1937 he joined the Otis Elevator Company, 935 Avenue Road, where he is at present employed. Applicant has lived in China from his early childhood and does not speak Russian. While in Hankow he was a member of the British Volunteer Corps. He is not registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee, nor the Russian Public Organisation in Shanghai (SORO), nor the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau, He resides at 1522, House 14, Bubbling Well Road. Tel.36105. Nothing detrimental is known by this office against the applicant.

Victor Semenovich Nechaeff, Russian, was born on
April 18, 1914, at Chita Transbaikal Province, Siberia. His
father professionally is a mining engineer but worked in
Manchuria for some time as a contractor. He is at present
unemployed and resides in Harbin. Nechaeff arrived in
Manchuria between 1920-1921 and later removed to Imianpo
Station, Chinese Eastern Railway. Applicant attended the
Imianpo Primary School leaving there in 1926. In the latter
part of 1926 Nechaeff arrived in Shanghai from Manchuria with
his elder brother and continued his education, for a few months,
in the Public & Thomas Hanbury School for Boys, 191 North
Szechuen Road, afterwards attending the St Joan of Arc's
College, 19 Route Doumer. In 1929 Nechaeff left that school
and from January 1930 was employed by Anderson and Ferroggiaro,
775 Avenue Foch, until in 1934 he left of his own accord.
From April, 1934 to August, 1935 he was employed with Cathay
Motors Limited, 271 Medhurst Road, when he was paid off on
the firm reducing its staff. In September, 1935 Nechaeff
obtained a position as a mechanic with Richards Auto Works,
101 Avenue du Roi Albert, and is still employed there.
He resides at 101 Avenue du Roi Albert with his
younger, adopted brother, A.S. Nechaeff, who is employed as
an apprentice with Richards Auto Works. Nechaeff is registered
with the Russian Emigrants Committee. Nothing detrimental is
known by this office against the applicant.

维克多·谢苗诺维奇·涅恰耶夫（Victor Semenovich Nechaeff），俄国人，1914年4月18日出生于西伯利亚外贝加尔省赤塔。其父职业为采矿工程师，但曾在满洲里担任承包商一段时间。目前失业，居住在哈尔滨。涅恰耶夫于1920-1921年间抵达满洲里，后迁至中东铁路伊绵坡站（Imianpo Station）。申请人就读于伊绵坡小学，于1926年离校。1926年下半年，涅恰耶夫与其兄长从满洲里抵达上海，并在北四川路191号的公立汤恩伯利男校（Public & Thomas Hanbury School for Boys）继续学业数月，随后就读于杜美路19号的圣贞德学院（St Joan of Arc's College）。1929年，涅恰耶夫离开该校，自1930年1月起受雇于福煦路775号的安德森与费罗贾罗公司（Anderson and Ferroggiaro），直至1934年自行离职。1934年4月至1935年8月，他受雇于麦特赫斯特路271号的国泰汽车有限公司（Cathay Motors Limited），后因公司裁员而被解雇。1935年9月，涅恰耶夫在阿尔伯特王路101号的理查兹汽车修造厂（Richards Auto Works）获得机械师职位，并至今仍在此任职。

Subject T. H. Moller, applicant to join the S.M.P. (Specials).
Made by D. J. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by C Gandon

Tage Hannested Moller, Danish subject, was born on
November 6th, 1898 in Eastern Siberia. His father was for-
merly connected with a Danish firm in Russia, exporting butter
and importing agricultural machinery. At present he is em-
ployed in a firm in Copenhagen, Denmark. Applicant was
educated in a Middle School in Copenhagen. Later he was
employed for various periods as a shop assistant with different
firms in Copenhagen. From 1923 to 1924 he worked as a sailor
on the s.s. "Palestria". In April 1924 he arrived in Shanghai
on board the above vessel and signed off on his own accord.
In Shanghai he was employed with the Shanghai Milk Supply Co.,
145 Tunsin Road, for several months, after which he joined
the China Car & Foundry Co., Ltd, 31 Yuen Ming Yuen Road, and
has since been employed at this firm's factory situated at
Kwong Foo Road, Chapei (near North Ferry Road).
Moller is registered with the local Danish Consulate-
General and resides at 1017 Bubbling Well Road, with his wife
and two daughters.
Nothing detrimental is known by this office against the
applicant.

D. J. Tcheremshansky

塔格·汉内斯泰德·莫勒（Tage Hannested Moller），丹麦籍，1898年11月6日出生于西伯利亚东部。其父曾供职于俄国的一家丹麦商行，从事黄油出口和农业机械进口业务。目前他在丹麦哥本哈根的一家公司任职。申请人在哥本哈根的一所中学接受教育。后来，他在哥本哈根的不同公司断续担任店员。1923年至1924年，他在“Palestria”号轮船上担任海员。1924年4月，他乘坐上述船只抵达上海，并自行离船。
在上海，他先在通新路145号的上海牛奶供应公司（Shanghai Milk Supply Co.）工作了几个月，随后加入圆明园路31号的中国汽车铸造有限公司（China Car & Foundry Co., Ltd），此后一直受雇于该公司位于闸北广福路（近北浮桥路）的工厂。

Made by D.S.Pavloff    Forwarded by R W Mac Auley D.S.I.

Bruno ITALIENER, German Jew, was born on February
18, 1891 in Altona, Germany. He arrived in Shanghai
from Germany on October 1, 1931 and in November of the
same year established himself as a manufacturers'
representative with an office at 114, Kiangse Road. In
July 1937 he moved his office to Room 210, 255 Peking
Road. At present he represents various English and
Belgian firms such as H.R. Feather & Company, Bedford,
England, Piltzer & Fils, Brussels, Belgium, etc.
The applicant is registered with the German
Consulate-General and holds passport No. 378/37 issued
on October 21, 1937.
There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to his character.

Subject L. B. Evstafieff alias Leo Eustaff, applicant to join the S.M.P.

Made by D. S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by C. Gandel
With reference to the attached recruiting form of Leo Eustaff,
enquiries elicit the following information :-
The correct name of the applicant is Leonid Borisovich
Evstafieff. He is a Russian who was born on October 11, 1912
at Hankow. His father who was formerly employed with the
Municipal Police of the Russian Concession in Hankow, joined
the Russian Army during the Great War and is reported to have
been missing since.
L. Evstafieff and his brother Peter Evstafieff, being
orphans, are reported to have been brought up by Catholic
missionaries and later adopted the Roman Catholic religion.
The applicant received his education first in the St. Mary's
College in Hankow and subsequently in the St. Xavier's College
in Shanghai, after which in 1926, he and his brother were sent
to Turin, Italy to continue their studies in a Ecclesia-
stical Seminary. The two brothers returned to Shanghai in
1929 as, according to their own statements, they did not wish
to become clergymen.
Upon his return to Shanghai, L. Evstafieff was for a
few weeks employed as an assistant teacher in the St. Xavier's
College, after which he worked for about two years with the
Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury, being attached to the
Editorial Office. Subsequently he joined the "Studio d'art",
Bubbling Well Road, which firm he left after eight months service.
In 1932 he was employed for about five months with the Black
and Baltic Seas Insurance Company (a Soviet owned firm), after
which he worked for a short period as a salesman with the Cathay
Ceramic Works, 24 The Bund. Since March 1, 1936, he has been
employed as a clerk and assistant accountant with the Societe

据报，L. 叶夫斯塔菲耶夫及其弟彼得·叶夫斯塔菲耶夫（Peter Evstafieff）身为孤儿，由天主教传教士抚养长大，后信奉罗马天主教。申请人先在汉口的圣玛丽亚学院（St. Mary's College）接受教育，随后在上海的圣方济各沙勿略学院（St. Xavier's College）就读，之后于1926年，他和弟弟被送往意大利都灵，在一所神学院继续学业。两兄弟于1929年返回上海，据他们自己陈述，是因为他们不愿成为神职人员。
回到上海后，L. 叶夫斯塔菲耶夫在圣方济各沙勿略学院担任助理教师数周，随后在《上海晚邮报与水星报》（Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury）编辑部工作约两年。之后，他加入静安寺路的“艺术工作室”（Studio d'art），服务八个月后离职。1932年，他在黑海与波罗的海保险公司（一家苏维埃所有的公司）工作约五个月，随后在外滩24号的国泰陶瓷厂（Cathay Ceramic Works）短暂担任推销员。自1936年3月1日起，他受雇于

    Evstafieff was a member of the American Company, S.V.C.
from 11.10.31 to 21.6.32. When joining the company he falsely
stated that he was an American, born in San Francisco. On
13.4.32 he was arrested on a charge of having stolen from the
S.V.C. Club one overcoat, value $66.00, property of W.N. Cochran,
an employee of Kelly & Walsh Co. For this offence he was
sentenced by the Shanghai First Special District Court on
21.4.32 to two months imprisonment. It is of interest to
note that upon his arrest he stated that he was employed with
Kunst & Albers Co. Subsequent enquiries proved that he had
never worked in the firm.
    In July 1936 Evstafieff made an unsuccessful application
to join the Transport Company S.V.C. It must be noted that
in his statement in his enrolment form he mentioned that he
was an employee of the China General Omnibus Company, which
was incorrect, as he never was connected with that company.
Being interviewed in connection with this matter, Evstafieff
stated that he had been advised by Captain P. W. Ingmer of the
Transport Company to mention the Omnibus Company as his place
of employment because it could help him to join the Transport
Company in which, as a rule, Russians are not admitted.
    Peter Evstafieff, the applicant's brother, first came to
notice of the Municipal Police on 24.4.33 when he was sentenced
to 6 months imprisonment by the Shanghai Special District Court
for misappropriation(sentence suspended for 3 years). On
19.7.34 he was brought before the same court on a charge of

九江路150号的比利时在华铁路公司（Belge de Chemins de Fer en Chine），该公司是乌科梅塔尔公司（Ucometal，即比利时联合冶金商业联盟 Union Commercial Belge de Metallurgie）及其他几家公司的代理。
    叶夫斯塔菲耶夫于1931年10月11日至1932年6月21日期间是商团（S.V.C.）美国连的成员。加入该连时，他虚假声称自己是美国人，出生于旧金山。1932年4月13日，他因涉嫌从商团俱乐部盗窃一件价值66.00美元的大衣（系凯利与沃尔什公司员工 W.N. Cochran 的财产）而被捕。为此罪行，他于1932年4月21日被上海第一特区地方法院判处两个月监禁。值得注意的是，被捕时他声称受雇于孔斯特与阿尔伯斯公司（Kunst & Albers Co.）。随后的调查证明他从未在该公司工作过。
    1936年7月，叶夫斯塔菲耶夫申请加入商团运输连未果。必须指出的是，他在入伍表的陈述中提到他是中国公共汽车公司（China General Omnibus Company）的员工，这是不实的，因为他从未与该公司有过关联。就此事项接受问询时，叶夫斯塔菲耶夫称，商团运输连的 P. W. Ingmer 上尉建议他提及公共汽车公司作为其雇主，因为这有助于他加入通常不招收俄国人的运输连。
    申请人的弟弟彼得·叶夫斯塔菲耶夫首次引起工部局警务处注意是在1933年4月24日，当时他因挪用公款被上海特区地方法院判处6个月监禁（缓刑3年）。1934年7月19日，他因

Boris Moiseyevich Lipkovsky, Russian of Jewish
origin, was born on February 2, 1916 at Yekaterinburg, Russia.
In 1917 he left Russia for Japan together with his parents
and in 1920 arrived in Shanghai. Applicant was educated at
the Public & Thomas Hanbury School for Boys graduating in
1932. In 1927 he made a six months trip to Europe with his
mother and sister, during which time he visited Belgium,
France and other countries. In 1930 he again visited Europe
and the United States together with his mother. In 1933 he
was employed with Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer of China, Room 138/41,
Embankment Building. In 1935 he worked for a period with
Triangle Motors Fed. Inc., U.S.A., 99 Route Cardinal Mercier.
In 1936 Lipkovsky left for Dairen where he was
employed with the Belgian Industrial Delegation for four
months. In 1937 he returned to Shanghai and has since been
working in the Cathay Jewellery, 272 Kiangse Road owned by
his father and a certain O. Mironoff, Russian of Jewish origin.
During the present Sino-Japanese hostilities Lipkovsky
temporarily joined the Transport Company, S.V.C.
Applicant is registered with the Shanghai City
Government Police Bureau as a Russian emigrant and resides
Lane
at/1220 Avenue Road, House 57. He is a member of the
Jewish Recreation Club and of the Shanghai Recreation Club.
Nothing detrimental is known by this office against
the applicant.

notice of the Municipal Police in 1927-1931 in connection
with drug smuggling and in 1932 in connection with the
smuggling of jewellery and on the whole does not enjoy

With reference to the attached application received from
Mr. Alfred John HEADINGTON, British, for enrolment, in the
S.M.P. (Specials), I have to report that this individual was appointed a
Probationary Sergeant on probation in the Shanghai Municipal
Police on January 1, 1929. His services were dispensed
with on February 23, 1929 following numerous complaints
received regarding his conduct whilst in the Gordon Road Training
Depot. It was considered that he would not become an efficient
police officer as he lacked balance and had no sense of
responsibility. Apart from the foregoing, nothing detrimental
is known against the applicant.

Subject J.J. Menishkis, N.P. Nosoreff and J.P. Lazareff - applicants to
join the S.M.P. (Specials).
Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Crawford
（印：18 OCT. 1937）
1. Joseph J. Menishkis, Lithuanian, was born on December 20,
1920 at Shanghai. He attended the St. Francis Xavier's College
for six years and the Public & Hos. Hanbury School for Boys
for one year. Upon leaving the latter school in 1936 he has
been assisting in his father's business.
J.J. Menishkis, the applicant's father, has been resident
in Shanghai since 1920 during which period he has been the pro-
prietor of a watch and jewellery shop at present situated at
671 Bubbling Well Road. From 1922 J.J. Menishkis has been the
Lithuanian Representative in Shanghai and in this capacity of-
ten rendered assistance to the Municipal Police in connection
with enquiries concerning his nationals.
2. Nicolai Pavlovich NOSOREFF, Russian, was born on December 4,
1901 at Samara, Russia. Upon graduating from a middle school at
Samara in 1918 he joined as a volunteer the "White" army. In
1920, following the collapse of Admiral Kolchak's government in
Siberia, he went to China and subsequently resided in Harbin
where he studied at the Polytechnic Institute. Graduating in
1925 he worked in his professional capacity in Harbin until
1932 when he left for Shanghai. Here he was employed with the
Studio d'art, 126 Bubbling Well Road for about four years, after
which he was unemployed for one year. In July, 1936 he joined
Palmer & Turner, 17 Canton Road. He is still employed with the
latter firm, but on October 1 received a notice to the effect
that his services would be dispensed with on November 1, 1937.
Mr. J.L. Patterson, chief engineer of Palmer & Turner, interviewed
by the undersigned in connection with this matter, stated that
the applicant's service was quite satisfactory and that the

由 D.S.I. Prokofiev 撰写。由 C. Crawford 转呈
（印：1937年10月18日）
1. 约瑟夫·J·梅尼什基斯 (Joseph J. Menishkis)，立陶宛人，1920年12月20日出生于上海。他就读于圣方济各沙勿略学院 (St. Francis Xavier's College) 六年，并在汉伯里公立及医院男子学校 (Public & Hos. Hanbury School for Boys) 就读一年。1936年离开该校后，他一直协助父亲经营生意。
申请人 J.J. 梅尼什基斯的父亲自1920年起定居上海，在此期间，他一直是位于静安寺路671号的一家钟表珠宝店的店主。自1922年起，J.J. 梅尼什基斯担任上海立陶宛代表，并在此职位上经常就涉及其本国国民的调查事项向工部局警务处提供协助。
2. 尼古拉·帕夫洛维奇·诺索列夫 (Nicolai Pavlovich NOSOREFF)，俄罗斯人，1901年12月4日出生于俄罗斯萨马拉。1918年从萨马拉的一所中学毕业后，他志愿加入了“白军”。1920年，随着西伯利亚高尔察克海军上将政府的垮台，他前往中国，随后居住在哈尔滨，并在那里的高等理工学院学习。1925年毕业后，他在哈尔滨从事专业工作，直到1932年前往上海。此后，他在静安寺路126号的 Studio d'art 工作了约四年，之后失业一年。1936年7月，他加入广东路17号的培格洋行 (Palmer & Turner)。他目前仍受雇于该商行，但于10月1日收到通知，称其服务将于1937年11月1日终止。
培格洋行总工程师 J.L. 帕特森 (Mr. J.L. Patterson) 就此事接受本署人员问询时表示，申请人的工作表现相当令人满意，并且

According to Lazareff ,he is making arrangements for the

3. Constantin Petrovich Lazareff, Russian, was born on February
20,1910 at Nicolsk-Ussuriysk, Maritime Province,Russia. He stu-
died at the St. Joseph's College at Yokohama until 1925,after
which he continued his education at a middle school in Harbin,
graduating in 1926. In 1928 he came to Shanghai. Here he was
employed as a radio mechanic and salesman with the Electric Ser-
vice Corporation,20 Nanking Road, from 1928 to 1933 when this
firm was closed. He then was employed with the American Engineer-
ing Corporation,909 Bubbling Well Road,for about one year as a
salesman, after which he worked independently in the same capa-
city for a period. In 1935-1936 he was employed as a salesman
with the Radio Equipment Co., 271 Kiangsi Road and in October,
1936 joined the Victor Radio Sales Co.,909 Bubbling Well Road
as a sales manager. From August,1937 he has been working for the
latter firm only on a commission basis.

Lazareff served with the Light Gun Battery ,S.V.C.,
from 1933 to 1935.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee,
118/1 Moulmein Road, and resides at 61/20 Route de Grouchy.

据拉扎列夫 (Lazareff) 称，他正安排与另一位名为 A.F. 马申 (A.F. Mashin) 的俄罗斯人合伙，于1937年11月1日前在静安寺路以“联合无线电” (Union Radio) 的名义建立自己的商行。
拉扎列夫已在俄罗斯联合组织委员会 (CURO) 注册，并与妻子和女儿共同居住于葛罗希路 (Route de Grouchy) 56-A号。

3. 康斯坦丁·彼得罗维奇·拉扎列夫 (Constantin Petrovich Lazareff)，俄罗斯人，1910年2月20日出生于俄罗斯滨海边疆区乌苏里斯克 (Nicolsk-Ussuriysk)。他在横滨的圣约瑟夫学院 (St. Joseph's College) 学习至1925年，随后在哈尔滨的一所中学继续学业，并于1926年毕业。1928年他来到上海。此后，他在南京路20号的电力服务公司 (Electric Service Corporation) 担任无线电技师和销售员，从1928年工作至1933年该公司关闭。随后，他在静安寺路909号的美国工程公司 (American Engineering Corporation) 担任销售员约一年，之后以相同身份独立工作了一段时间。1935年至1936年间，他在江西路271号的无线电设备公司 (Radio Equipment Co.) 担任销售员，并于1936年10月加入静安寺路909号的胜利无线电销售公司 (Victor Radio Sales Co.) 担任销售经理。自1937年8月起，他仅以佣金制方式为后者工作。

拉扎列夫于1933年至1935年间在上海义勇军 (S.V.C.) 轻炮连服役。

他在莫尔缅路 (Moulmein Road) 118/1号的俄罗斯难民委员会注册，居住于葛罗希路 (Route de Grouchy) 61/20号。

Subject S.A. Kovaleff - applicant to join the S.M.P. (Specials).

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. [Signature]

Sergey Alexandrovich KOVALEFF, Russian, was born on
July 4, 1898 in Amur Province, Siberia, and is the son of an offi-
cer of the Russian Imperial Army who later served as a school of-
ficial in Transbaikal Province, Siberia. The applicant received
his education at a middle school in Chita and in the Blagoveschensk
Technicum. In 1919-1921 during the civil war in Siberia he serv-
ed in the ranks of the "White" army and is reported to have been
wounded and shell-shocked. Following the defeat of the "Whites"
Kovaleff arrived in Harbin where he subsequently worked as a
draughtsman and painter for some time. In 1923 he was employed
at the Asian Sifan Railway for 6 months as a railway engineer.
He then returned to Harbin and worked as a painter until February
1925, when he left for Shanghai. Here he obtained employment with
L.E. Hudec, local architect, with whom he worked for one year. At
the same time he worked for Brandt & Rogers, 15 Szechuen Road.
In 1927 Kovaleff left for Tsinanfu, Shantung, where he was appointed
assistant manager of the Arsenal of Marshal Chang Chung Chang's
army. After several months' service in this capacity he returned
to Shanghai and worked as a draughtsman for about one year with
J. Arbvoss, 354 Avenue Haig and then from 1929 to 1933 with Hazzard
& Elliott, 33 Szechuen Road. From March 1, 1934 till April 30 of
the same year he was employed as a supervisor with the Public
Works Department of the French Municipality which service, it is
reported, he was obliged to leave after it had been discovered
that he accepted bribes. In 1934-35 he was employed with the
Modern Home Construction Supplies, Ltd, 1110 Gordon Road, and in
1935-1936 with Graham & Painter, 668 Szechuen Road. From October,
1936 until the outbreak of the present hostilities in Shanghai
he was employed with Palmer & Turner, 17 Canton Road, after which

谢尔盖·亚历山德罗维奇·科瓦列夫 (Sergey Alexandrovich KOVALEFF)，俄罗斯人，1898年7月4日出生于西伯利亚阿穆尔省，系一名俄罗斯帝国陆军军官之子，其父后来在西伯利亚外贝加尔省担任学校官员。申请人在赤塔的一所中学和布拉戈维申斯克技术学校接受教育。1919年至1921年西伯利亚内战期间，他在“白军”中服役，据报曾受伤并患有炮弹休克症。“白军”战败后，科瓦列夫抵达哈尔滨，随后在那里担任绘图员和画家一段时间。1923年，他在亚洲西番铁路 (Asian Sifan Railway) 担任铁路工程师6个月。随后他返回哈尔滨，继续做画家，直到1925年2月前往上海。在此地，他受雇于当地建筑师 L.E. 邬达克 (L.E. Hudec)，为其工作了一年。同时，他为四川路15号的 Brandt & Rogers 工作。1927年，科瓦列夫前往山东济南府，被任命为张宗昌元帅军队兵工厂的副经理。在此职位服务数月后，他返回上海，在海格路354号的 J. Arbvoss 处担任绘图员约一年，随后从1929年至1933年在四川路33号的 Hazzard & Elliott 工作。从1934年3月1日至同年4月30日，他受雇于法公董局工务处担任监工，据报后因被发现收受贿赂而被迫离职。1934年至1935年，他受雇于戈登路1110号的现代家居建筑用品有限公司 (Modern Home Construction Supplies, Ltd)，1935年至1936年受雇于四川路668号的 Graham & Painter。从1936年10月至上海当前战事爆发前，他受雇于广东路17号的培格洋行 (Palmer & Turner)，此后

he has been without a regular employment. Mr. J.L. Patterson,
Chief Engineer of Palmer & Turner, interviewed by the undersigned,
stated that Novaleff' services had been quite satisfactory and
that he had been discharged on account of a reduction in staff.
It is reported that from 1933, owing to an unsuccessful
business venture, Novaleff has been heavily indebted and that in
this connection he was in trouble with his creditors on several
occasions. He admits that he still has about $ 1,000 unpaid
debts.
On August 23, 1935 he attempted to commit suicide by
shooting himself through the chest from a pistol in the Jess-

to take his life in 1933 owing to financial difficulties and
family trouble.
Novaleff states that he served in the S.M.P. (Specials)
for about two months during the Sino-Japanese hostilities in
1932.
He is registered with the Russian Emigrants Committee
and resides at 223/2 Route des Soeurs together with his wife and
daughter.
On the whole Novaleff does not seem to be a suitable
person for the service with the S.M.P. (Specials).
