Date 20th Oct. 1937
Subject Jellinek - Applicant to join the S.M.P. (Specials).
Made by A.A. Ivanov. Forwarded by C. Ganson (V.O.)

Alfred Wilhelm JELLINEK, Czechoslovakian of Jewish
origin, states that he was born on March 11, 1902 at Iglau, Czecho-
slovakia, and that he is a chemical engineer by profession. He
arrived in Shanghai during the autumn of 1932 coming from Siam
via Japan. According to him, he was at that time on a round-the-
world tour as a correspondent of several newspapers including
the "Leipziger Abendblatt" (Leipzig), "Ost-Oesterreichische Post"
(Austria) and "Tuerkische Post" (Constantinople).
Shortly after his arrival here he was engaged by the lo-
cal German newspaper "Deutsche Shanghai Zeitung" as a town re-
porter, in which capacity he worked for several months. From March,
1933 to the later part of 1934 he was the editor of the "Green
Post", a fortnightly magazine in English, French, German and Chinese
languages with the editorial office at 424 Burkill Road. It was
reported that the publication was financed by a certain Dr. Liang
Tsin Jung, who resided at the above address and who, in turn, re-
ceived the money from the "Sun Fo clique". However, the magazine
in question did not come to the notice of the Municipal Police in
connection with any political propaganda.
After the publication of the "Green Post" had been dis-
continued, Jellinek worked with the AUTOMIN WORKS, 80 Miaochow
Road, for about one year as a salesman. Following the closure of
this firm he worked in the same capacity independently for a pe-
riod. At present he claims to be a partner of the China Universal
Engineers, 169 Yuen Ming Yuen Road. Mr. A. Quoika, manager of the
said firm, interviewed by the undersigned, stated that Jellinek
was only allowed to use the company's office and occasionally
also worked for them on a commission basis.
Enquiries at the local Czechoslovakian Consulate show

Alfred Wilhelm JELLINEK，捷克籍，犹太裔，称其于1902年3月11日出生于捷克斯洛伐克的伊格劳（Iglau），职业为化学工程师。他于1932年秋季从暹罗经日本抵达上海。据其自称，当时他正以多家报纸通讯员的身份进行环球旅行，这些报纸包括《莱比锡晚报》（Leipziger Abendblatt，莱比锡）、《奥地利东部邮报》（Ost-Oesterreichische Post，奥地利）和《土耳其邮报》（Tuerkische Post，君士坦丁堡）。
抵达上海后不久，他被当地德文报纸《德文上海报》（Deutsche Shanghai Zeitung）聘为城市新闻记者，在此职位上工作了数月。从1933年3月至1934年下半年，他担任《绿邮报》（Green Post）的编辑，这是一份以英、法、德、中四种语言出版的半月刊，编辑部位于伯基尔路（Burkill Road）424号。据报道，该出版物由一位名叫梁金荣（Liang Tsin Jung，音译）博士的人资助，此人居住在上述地址，而其资金又来自“孙佛系”（Sun Fo clique，即孙科派系）。然而，该杂志并未因任何政治宣传活动而引起工部局警务处的注意。
《绿邮报》停刊后，Jellinek在苗州路（Miaochow Road，音译）80号的AUTOMIN工厂（音译）工作了约一年，担任销售员。在该商行关闭后，他以同样的身份独立工作了一段时间。目前，他声称是圆明园路169号中国通用工程公司（China Universal Engineers）的合伙人。经本署人员询问，该公司经理A. Quoika先生表示，仅允许Jellinek使用公司办公室，并偶尔以佣金为基础为公司工作。

that although Jellinek has been residing in Shanghai for five
years it was not until the end of August, 1937 that he came to
the consulate for registration. On that occasion he wore the
uniform of the S.M.Police (Specials). Producing a certificate
of nationality, he applied for a passport. As the consulate
has on file a circular issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs,
Czechoslovakia, on 1-7-30 to the effect that A.J.Jellinek was
wanted by the judicial authorities to answer certain charges of
fraud and forgery of passport, he was told that a passport valid
for three months would be granted to him on the condition that
he would immediately proceed to Czechoslovakia in order to clear
himself of the said charges. Since that time Jellinek has not
been seen at the consulate. On the whole he is regarded by the
consular staff with suspicion and is not considered by them a
suitable candidate for service in the police.
Interviewed by the undersigned Jellinek gave very
evasive replies regarding the matter of his registration with
the local Czechoslovakian consulate. Inter alia, he made a
hint that the German elements in Czechoslovakia were not receiv-
ing a fair treatment from the government of that country. He
also mentioned that he had secured a seven years' agreement
with the Nanking Government in connection with some work of a mi-
litary significance and that from November 1, 1937 he would be
considered a Chinese citizen. According to him, this was necessary
in order to protect him against the possibility of reprisals on the
part of the Japanese should he fall into their hands.
Jellinek resides at House 1, Lane 147, Avenue Haig.
While in Shanghai he did not come to the notice of
the Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an un-
desirable character.
D.C.(Special Branch) Copy sent to D.S.I. (Specials) S.R.

尽管Jellinek已在上海居住五年，但直到1937年8月底他才前往领事馆登记。当时他身穿工部局警务处（特别队）制服。他出示了国籍证明，并申请护照。由于领事馆存档中有捷克斯洛伐克外交部于1930年7月1日发布的一份通告，指出A.J. Jellinek因某些欺诈和伪造护照的指控而被司法机关通缉，因此被告知，条件是他必须立即前往捷克斯洛伐克以洗清上述指控，方可获发有效期为三个月的护照。自那以后，领事馆未再见到Jellinek。总体而言，领事馆工作人员对他持怀疑态度，并认为他不适合担任警务人员。
经本署人员询问，Jellinek就其在当地捷克斯洛伐克领事馆登记一事给出了非常含糊的回答。其间，他暗示捷克斯洛伐克的德意志元素未受到该国政府的公平对待。他还提到，他已与南京政府就某些具有军事意义的工作达成了为期七年的协议，并且从1937年11月1日起，他将被视为中国公民。据其称，这是必要的，以便万一落入日本人手中时，保护自己免受日方报复的可能性。
Jellinek居住在海格路（Avenue Haig）147弄1号。
在上海期间，他未因任何不良性质的活动而引起工部局警务处的注意。

REPORT
Date October 25, 37.

Subject A. Pfeifer - applicant to join the Shanghai Municipal Police (Specials).

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by C. [Signature]

With reference to verbal instructions of P.A. to
D.C. (Special Branch) re further report regarding A. Pfeifer,
I have to state that, according to information confidentially
obtained from the local German Consulate-General (Mr. H. Getjen,
Chief Chancellor, and Mr. von Ladow), Pfeifer for some time was
financially embarassed, but he settled these money affairs
and nothing detrimental is known against him. However, further
enquiries show that the statement of the officials of German
Consulate General was not correct. On August 1, 1936, Pfeifer
absconded from a boarding house known as "Bubbling Well Court"
situated at No. 178, Lane 591 Bubbling Well Road, owing $136.85
for boarding and lodging. According to the statement of
Mrs. Roberts, French, manageress of the above boarding house,
a clerk of this establishment visited the German Consulate-
General and complained against Pfeifer for non-payment of the
bill. As a result of this complaint, Pfeifer promised to
settle the account in a few days, but has not been seen since.
Evidently, the German Consular officials were under the
impression that Pfeifer had settled the matter as the clerk of
the boarding house in question did not make any further complaint
against Pfeifer.

（印：... B. ... 402）

g Tcheremshansky
D. S.

Getjen先生和von Ladow先生）秘密获得的信息，Pfeifer曾在一段时间内陷入财务困境，但他已解决这些金钱事务，且未发现对其不利的情况。然而，进一步调查显示，德国总领事馆官员的陈述并不正确。1936年8月1日，Pfeifer因拖欠食宿费136.85美元，从位于静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）591弄178号的一家名为“静安别墅”（Bubbling Well Court，音译）的寄宿公寓潜逃。据上述寄宿公寓的法籍经理Roberts夫人称，该机构的一名职员曾前往德国总领事馆投诉Pfeifer未支付账单。作为此次投诉的结果，Pfeifer承诺在几天内结清账目，但此后便杳无音信。显然，德国领事官员以为Pfeifer已解决此事，因为该寄宿公寓的职员未再对Pfeifer提出任何投诉。

Evald Otto Carl George Kolshorn, German, was born on December
28, 1907 at Altona, Germany. His father was a Railway official.
Applicant received his education in Altona Gymnasium graduating
in 1923, after which he was employed with George Hanne Export Co.
in Hamburg. In 1928 Kolshorn left for Shanghai and was employed
with the Sino-Foreign M.M. Export Co. for one year. In 1930
he joined the Cosmos Paper Co. Fed. Inc. U.S.A., Hamilton House,
Rooms 240-242, where he is still employed. Kolshorn is a
member of the German Garden Club. He resides at No. 125A Avenue
du Roi Albert, House 11(Verdun Terrace).

Arthur Pfeifer, German, was born on December 14, 1901 at
Tientsin. His late father was a merchant. Applicant was
educated in the Public and Thomas Hanbury School for Boys in
Shanghai, graduating in 1918. Later for about three years, he
was employed with various firms in Shanghai. In 1921 Pfeifer
left for Germany where he received a position as a teacher of
English in a Government Normal School in Hamburg. About two
years ago he lost this position and returned to Shanghai, where
he was employed for various periods with Millington Ltd., 668
Szechuen Road, The Mercury Press, 21 Avenue Edward VII, and
The United States Life Insurance Company of the City of New
York, 17 The Bund. About 6 months ago Pfeifer joined Frost
Bland & Co. Ltd, 33 Szechuen Road, where he is still employed.
His younger brother, Mr. B. Pfeifer has been employed for
many years with the Office Appliance Co., 150 Nanking Road.
His mother resides in Shanghai and his sister is a nun in one
of the local convents.
Pfeifer resides at No. 8 Yang Terrace.

Nauheim, Germany. He was educated in a Normal School in Hemnitz

and three other German firms.

GRIGORY Vladimirovich LVOFF, Russian, was born on January 7,
1905 at Moscow. He is reported to have left Russia for China in
1920 and to have subsequently resided in Harbin, where upon com-
pleting his education in one of the local schools he worked as
a salesman with Shriro Bros., Import & Export Co. Towards the end
of 1929 he resigned from this firm and was for a period employed
as a clerk with the Harbin branch of the National City Bank of
New York. Shortly after he left this position he, together with
two others, Choolkoff and Melgunoff, who were also employed at the
same bank, was implicated in defrauding the bank by drawing out
money on false cheques, for which offence he was subsequently sen-
tenced to 3 months imprisonment.

In August 1930 he came to Shanghai and soon afterwards
secured employment with the Shanghai Telephone Co. His services
with the company terminated in December 1931 due to his bank af-
fairs in Harbin reaching the ears of the management.

His next employment was with the Russian newspaper "Slovo",
Advertising Department, 238 Avenue du Roi Albert, where he worked
until September, 1932 when he left on his own accord.

In 1933-1934 he worked at various places as a tailor and
ladies hair-dresser apprentice respectively. In 1935-1936 he
conducted the Shanghai-Tsingtao Line, a travel agency located at
No 538 Avenue Joffre. This agency worked in conjunction with the
Jardine, Matheson & Co., Ltd. whose four freighters were converted
into passenger boats with the general idea of conveying Russian
on low tariffs during the summer season. During the same period
he also claims to have been engaged in commercial pursuits import-
ing silk materials in Shanghai. From February, 1937 he has been
working as a salesman on a commission basis for Messrs Olathe &

GRIGORY Vladimirovich LVOFF，俄国人，1905年1月7日出生于莫斯科。据报他于1920年离开俄国前往中国，随后居住在哈尔滨，在当地一所学校完成学业后，在Shriro Bros.进出口公司（音译）担任销售员。1929年底，他从该公司辞职，并在纽约国家城市银行（National City Bank of New York）哈尔滨分行担任职员一段时间。离职后不久，他与同样在该银行任职的Choolkoff和Melgunoff（均为音译）等两人一起，因涉嫌使用空头支票骗取银行资金而卷入案件，并因此罪行被判处三个月监禁。

1930年8月，他来到上海，并很快在上海电话公司找到工作。由于他在哈尔滨的银行事务传到了管理层耳中，他于1931年12月终止了在该公司的服务。

他的下一份工作是在阿尔伯特王路238号的俄文报纸《言论报》（Slovo）广告部，他一直工作到1932年9月，随后自愿离职。

1933-1934年间，他分别在多处担任裁缝和女士美发师学徒。1935-1936年间，他经营位于霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）538号的“上海-青岛线”旅行社。该旅行社与怡和洋行（Jardine, Matheson & Co., Ltd.）合作，将其四艘货轮改装为客轮，主要宗旨是在夏季以低票价运送俄国人。在同一时期，他还声称从事商业活动，在上海进口丝绸材料。从1937年2月起，他一直以佣金为基础为Olathe &

Subject R. Larsen - applicant to join the S.L.F. (Specials).

Made by D.S.Tcheremshansky Forwarded by [Signature]

Ricshard Larsen, Danish subject, was born on September 2,
1913 at Shanghai. He was educated at the St. Francis Xavier
College. Soon after leaving school he was engaged as a clerk
by the Great Northern Telegraph Company, 4 Avenue Edward VII,
where he worked from June 20, 1929 to June 12, 1934 when he had
to resign owing to reduction of staff and his inability to
master the Danish language. Apart from the latter fact, he
was considered a capable and honest worker. Later for about
one and half year Larsen was connected with the Roma florist
shop, 259 Avenue Haig, owned by his mother-in-law, Mrs. Frischen,
German. Subsequently, for a period he was unemployed. Since
May 1937 he started his own business under the style Tropicana
Pet Co., 172/13 Rue Admiral Courbet (breeding gold fish etc.)
in partnership with one J.E.Friberg, Swedish. On October 15 of
this year Larsen joined the International Guides Bureau, 180
Nanking Road, where he is now employed as a clerk.

Larsen resides with his wife at 473/4 Rue Ratard.

Nothing detrimental is known by this office against the applicant.

His late father Jacob Martin Larsen committed suicide
about the end of 1927 or early in 1928. He was known as an
arms smuggler and swindler. On January 24, 1924 he was
sentenced for Fraud to 20 days of imprisonment and on March 5,
1926 was again sentenced for Fraud to 30 days imprisonment.
On June 6, 1927 he was arrested on a warrant issued by the
Danish Consul and sentenced to 14 days detention on a charge
of failing to support his wife and family.

DSC

Ricshard Larsen，丹麦籍，1913 年 9 月 2 日出生于上海。他就读于圣方济各沙勿略学院 (St. Francis Xavier College)。毕业后不久，他被爱文义路 (Avenue Edward VII) 4 号的大北电报公司聘为职员，从 1929 年 6 月 20 日工作至 1934 年 6 月 12 日，后因裁员及无法掌握丹麦语而辞职。除后者外，他被视为一名能干且诚实的员工。此后约一年半，Larsen 在其岳母、德国人 Frischen 太太拥有的海格路 (Avenue Haig) 259 号 Roma 花店工作。随后，他失业了一段时间。自 1937 年 5 月起，他与瑞典人 J.E.Friberg 合伙，以 Tropicana Pet Co. 的名义在库尔贝海军上将路 (Rue Admiral Courbet) 172/13 号开始自己的生意（饲养金鱼等）。今年 10 月 15 日，Larsen 加入南京路 180 号的国际导游局 (International Guides Bureau)，目前受雇为职员。

Larsen 与妻子居住在拉塔德路 (Rue Ratard) 473/4 号。

本局未发现对该申请人不利的情况。

其已故父亲 Jacob Martin Larsen 于 1927 年底或 1928 年初自杀。他 known as 军火走私犯和骗子。1924 年 1 月 24 日，他因欺诈罪被判处监禁 20 天，1926 年 3 月 5 日再次因欺诈罪被判处监禁 30 天。1927 年 6 月 6 日，他因丹麦领事签发的逮捕令被捕，并因未能供养妻儿被判处拘留 14 天。

Subject V.A.Vassilieff and L.A.Korshoonoff, applicants to join the Shanghai
Municipal Police (Specials).

Made by D.S.Tcheremshansky Forwarded by

Victor Alexandrovich Vassilieff, Russian, was born on
January 11, 1903 at Vladivostok. His late father was a merchant.
He studied in Vladivostok Normal School and upon graduating in
1921 he left for Germany, where he continued his education in
the Darmstadt Polytechnicum. In 1927-1928 Vassilieff studied
in a Polytechnicum in Prague, Czecho-Slovakia. Later he was
employed for various periods with the Orion Machinery Factory,
Maxim Sheves Machinery Factory and the Film Department of
Luzerne Co. in Prague.
In 1934 Vassilieff arrived in Shanghai from Czecho-Slovakia
and opened here the Vivas Publicity Co. at Room 20A, Central
Arcade. He closed this firm in 1935 and was employed for a
period with Larsen & Trock, 178 Avenue Edward VII. In
December 1935 Vassilieff joined the "Slovo" Printing & Publishing
Co., 238 Avenue du Roi Albert. He left this firm three months
ago to join the Shanghai Times, 160 Avenue Edward VII, where
he is still employed as an advertising agent.
When in Czecho-Slovakia Vassilieff was a member of the
Union of Russian Students Organisation. He resided at 818-B
Avenue Joffre with his step-father Dr. S.Tomaszewski. His
elder brother is in U.S.A. and his younger brother L.Tomashevsky
adopted son of Dr. Tomaszewski, is employed with the French
Municipal Police. Applicants mother and sister reside at Harbin.
In January, 1935 Vassilieff joined the S.M.P.(Specials),
but after two months service resigned on his own accord.
Vassilieff is registered with the Russian Emigrants
Committee.
Nothing detrimental is known by this office against the
applicant.

Victor Alexandrovich Vassilieff，俄国人，1903 年 1 月 11 日出生于海参崴。其已故父亲是一名商人。他在海参崴师范学校学习，1921 年毕业后前往德国，在达姆施塔特理工学院继续深造。1927-1928 年，Vassilieff 在捷克斯洛伐克布拉格的一所理工学院学习。后来，他在布拉格的 Orion 机械厂、Maxim Sheves 机械厂和 Luzerne 公司电影部断续受雇。
1934 年，Vassilieff 从捷克斯洛伐克抵达上海，并在中央商场 (Central Arcade) 20A 室开设了 Vivas 广告公司。他于 1935 年关闭了该公司，并在爱文义路 (Avenue Edward VII) 178 号的 Larsen & Trock 公司工作了一段时间。1935 年 12 月，Vassilieff 加入阿尔贝国王路 (Avenue du Roi Albert) 238 号的“Slovo”印刷出版公司。三个月前他离开该公司，加入爱文义路 (Avenue Edward VII) 160 号的《上海泰晤士报》(Shanghai Times)，目前仍受雇为广告代理人。
在捷克斯洛伐克期间，Vassilieff 是俄国学生组织联盟的成员。他与继父 S.Tomaszewski 博士居住在霞飞路 (Avenue Joffre) 818-B 号。他的长兄在美国，弟弟 L.Tomashevsky 是 Tomaszewski 博士的养子，受雇于法租界公董局警务处。申请人的母亲和妹妹居住在哈尔滨。
1935 年 1 月，Vassilieff 加入工部局警务处（特别队），但在服役两个月后自愿辞职。
Vassilieff 已在俄国侨民委员会登记。
本局未发现对该申请人不利的情况。

Made by..D.S..Tcheremshansky...........Forwarded by....................

Mihail Alexeyevich Bentsianoff, Russian, was born on
July 25, 1908 at Irkutsk, Siberia. He left Russia for China
in 1922 together with his mother in order to join his father,
a brandy distiller by occupation, who had arrived in Harbin
previously. Applicant was educated in the Commercial and
subsequently in the Pushkin Schools in Harbin graduating in
1928. Later for about two years he was unemployed. From
1931 to 1932 he worked as an apprentice in Spirtenko's Vodka
Distillery in Harbin, where his father was employed. In 1932
he joined the Olma Chemicals Ltd. In 1933 he was transferred
to the Shanghai branch of the firm and since that time has been
attached as a chemist to their factory located at 200 Rue
Cassini.
Bentsianoff is a member of the Sports Committee of the
Russian Club, 1035 Avenue Foch. He is registered with the
Council of United Russian Organization in Shanghai (Soro) and
resides at No.25, flat 7, Route Tenant de la Tour.
（印：SPECIAL BRANCH SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE - 5 NOV 1937）
It is reported that in 1933 in Shanghai Bentsianoff was
on friendly terms and resided together with one Alexey Ivanovich
Stepanoff, 28, Soviet citizen, a building contractor by
occupation. The latter individual has the reputation of a
bolshevik sympathizer and is said to have been a member of the
Communist Youth Organization in Harbin. However, Bentsianoff
is not known to have any interest in politics and his connection
with Stepanoff may be accounted for by the fact that they
have known each other from childhood and also have common
interests as sportsmen and hunters.
Nothing detrimental is known by this office against the
applicant.
Copy to Dr (Specials) Tcheremshansky
D.C. (Special Branch) D.S.

米哈伊尔·阿列克谢耶维奇·本齐亚诺夫（Mihail Alexeyevich Bentsianoff），俄国人，1908年7月25日出生于西伯利亚伊尔库茨克。1922年，他与母亲一同离开俄国前往中国，以投奔此前已抵达哈尔滨的父亲，其父职业为白兰地蒸馏师。申请人在哈尔滨的商业学校就读，随后进入普希金学校，于1928年毕业。此后约两年处于失业状态。1931年至1932年间，他在哈尔滨的斯皮尔坚科（Spirtenko）伏特加蒸馏厂担任学徒，其父当时也受雇于此。1932年，他加入奥尔玛化工有限公司（Olma Chemicals Ltd.）。1933年，他被调至该公司上海分公司，自此以来一直作为化学师隶属于其位于盖司康路（Rue Cassini）200号的工厂。
本齐亚诺夫是霞飞路1035号俄国俱乐部体育委员会的成员。他在上海俄国侨民联合总会（Soro）登记注册，居住在 tenant de la Tour 路25号7室。
（印：特科 上海公共租界工部局警务处 - 1937年11月5日）
据报，1933年在上海期间，本齐亚诺夫与阿列克谢·伊万诺维奇·斯捷潘诺夫（Alexey Ivanovich Stepanoff）关系友好并共同居住。斯捷潘诺夫28岁，苏联公民，职业为建筑承包商。此人素有布尔什维克同情者的名声，据说曾是哈尔滨共产主义青年团的成员。然而，据知本齐亚诺夫对政治并无兴趣，他与斯捷潘诺夫的交往可归因于两人自幼相识，且作为运动员和猎人有共同的兴趣爱好。

Subject V.V.Volchkoff, applicant to join the S.M.P.(Specials)
Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by C. Crawford.

Vassily Vassilievich Volcnkoff, Russian, was born on May
24, 1914 at Chita Transbaikal Province, Siberia. His late father
was a Government official. Applicant arrived in Harbin from
Vladivostok in 1923 to join his parents who had left Russia
in 1921. In Harbin he attended a primary school for four
years and subsequently a high school for two years. Upon
leaving the school, he worked for various periods first as
an apprentice in a local barbershop, and later as a shop
assistant until 1931, when he left for Shanghai. Here he was
employed as a kennelman with the Canidrome, 432 Avenue du
Roi Albert, for one year and six months. In 1934 he worked
at Rosen's Beauty Parlour, 1005 Bubbling Well Road for 4
months, after which he left for Chefoo where he worked as a
hairdresser. Upon returning in Shanghai in 1935 he was
engaged by Backer's Beauty Parlour, Avenue Joffre where he
worked until May, 1937, after which he has been working at
C. Capelli's Hairdressing Salon, Room 224, Sassoon House.
Volchkoff was a member of the Russian Sporting Association
"Sokol" for two years. His mother, Mrs. E.S.Volcnkoff, resides
in Harbin. His brother, G.V.Volcnkoff, is a member of the
Russian Detachment, S.V.C.
Volchkoff is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee and resides at 204 Seymour Road, Apt 2 B.
Nothing detrimental is known by this office against the
applicant.

瓦西里·瓦西里耶维奇·沃尔奇科夫（Vassily Vassilievich Volcnkoff），俄国人，1914年5月24日出生于西伯利亚外贝加尔省赤塔。其已故父亲是一名政府官员。申请人于1923年从符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）抵达哈尔滨，与1921年离开俄国的父母团聚。在哈尔滨，他先读了四年小学，随后读了两年中学。离校后，他先后在不同时期担任当地理发店的学徒和店员，直到1931年离开前往上海。在此之后，他在阿尔伯特王路（Avenue du Roi Albert）432号的逸园跑狗场（Canidrome）担任犬只管理员一年零六个月。1934年，他在静安寺路1005号的罗森美容院（Rosen's Beauty Parlour）工作了4个月，随后前往烟台从事理发工作。1935年回到上海后，他受雇于霞飞路的贝克美容院（Backer's Beauty Parlour），工作至1937年5月，此后一直在沙逊大厦224室的C. Capelli美发沙龙工作。
沃尔奇科夫曾是俄国体育协会“索科尔”（Sokol）的成员，为期两年。其母E.S.沃尔奇科夫夫人居住在哈尔滨。其兄G.V.沃尔奇科夫是上海志愿团（S.V.C.）俄国分队的成员。
沃尔奇科夫已在俄国侨民委员会登记注册，居住在西摩路204号B座2室。

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.I.

Mihail Abramovich Lourie-Ettingaff, Soviet citizen
of Jewish origin, was born in 1888 at Novozybkov, Chernigov
Province, South Russia, and is the son of former well-to-do
merchant who owned sugar and lumber factories in Novozybkov.
Upon graduating from a local middle school he continued
his education in a German university. During the Great
War he joined the Russian Imperial Army as a volunteer
and, following the Russian Revolution in 1917, when Jews
were admitted in the military officers school, he entered
the Peterhof Military Officers School. It is said that
in the ranks of the school, he participated in the defence
of the Winter Palace in Petrograd against the bolsheviks.
In 1918 Lourie fled to Harbin where subsequently he
conducted the restaurant "Kishinev" and later a motor car
business in partnership with a certain Russian Jew named
Terk. Both enterprises were not successful. In 1925
Lourie entered the service of the Harbin Office of the
Chinese Eastern Railway, a Soviet enterprise. It is
believed that he received this position through the in-
fluence of the Soskin family, his relatives, owners of a
well known export firm in Harbin, which had business
connections with the Chinese Eastern Railway. In July,
1925, Lourie was transferred to the Shanghai agency of the
concern. In 1929 he resided at Hankow. In November 1930
he resigned from this position pleading ill health and,
it is reported, received a considerable sum from the
superannuation fund. He then became a partner of Topas
& Co. Ltd., 43 Szechuen Road, a real estate firm. In

Made by D.S.I. MacAdie Forwarded by Wogan A.S.S.

Henry Francis Parks, candidate for the Shanghai
Municipal Police (Specials) is a native of Washington
D.C. He first came to Shanghai in 1933 and engaged
in the photostat business, reproducing documents which
whenever he was doubtful of any of them, he submitted
to the Police for approval. He left Shanghai in 1937
for America, having been offered a good position in
the photography department of an aircraft firm. He
could not stay in the States, however as the Government
refused to recognize his wife (a Japanese). He returned
to Shanghai in March 1938 and joined the staff of the
Manufacturers Life Insurance Company.

He is a well known musician being formerly
connected with the Chicago Symphony Orchestra and is
now President of the Bohemian Club, an association
engaged in furthering local amateur musical culture.
The Club occasionally produces a concert at the Lyceum
Theatre for charitable purposes.

Nothing whatever is known to applicant's
detriment and his character and social life appear
to be above reproach.

Henry Francis Parks，上海公共租界工部局警务处（特别队）候选人，出生于华盛顿特区。他于 1933 年首次来到上海，从事静电复印业务，复制文件；每当他对任何文件存有疑虑时，都会提交给警方审批。1937 年，他因在一家飞机公司的摄影部门获得一个优厚职位而离开上海前往美国。然而，他无法在美国停留，因为政府不承认他的妻子（日本人）。他于 1938 年 3 月返回上海，并加入 Manufacturers Life Insurance Company（制造商人寿保险公司）的职员队伍。

他是一位知名的音乐家，此前曾与芝加哥交响乐团有联系，目前是 Bohemian Club（波希米亚俱乐部）的主席，该协会致力于促进本地业余音乐文化的发展。该俱乐部偶尔会在兰心大戏院举办慈善音乐会。

Wladimir Leonidovitch NOGOVIKOFF, Russian was born
in Simbirsk Province, Siberia, on November 22, 1914. He is
reported to have left Russia together with his family in

Shanghai for Tsingtao in August 1938 and returned here on
October 10, of the same year in the s.s. "Tsingtao Maru".
At present he is employed as a salesman with Wood Forwarders,
89 Foochow Road.

The applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road and there is nothing in the
Municipal Police records detrimental to his character.

Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. ...

A.B. ALVAREZ, first came to the notice of the Municipal Police on November 11, 1933, when he entered Flat No.304, Carter Road Police Quarters, and offered a radio aerial for sale. S.I. Harper who was the occupant of the flat at that time asked him to produce his business card which the applicant failed to do. After that he was taken to Sinza Police Station, where he was able to prove that the aerial belonged to his friend and that he was only trying to sell it for him, consequently no charge was preferred against A.B. Alvarez.

On July 22, 1934 a British lady came to the Dixwell Road Police Station and reported that her children aged from 5 to 14 years and their playmates were afraid to go to the Hongkew Park as they had been followed about by a foreigner, believed to be a Portuguese, who carried a raincoat over his arm, leaving his trousers unfastened and exposing his person to the children. On August 26, 1934 the children mentioned above came to Dixwell Road Police Station and stated that at about 6.30 p.m. when they were playing in the park, they saw the same foreigner, sitting and exposing his person to them. They demanded that he proceed to the Hongkew Park gate where S.P.C. 84 met them and escorted all concerned to the Station. At the Station the foreigner gave his name and address as Mr. A.B. Alvarez, Spanish, residing at 14, Dixwell Road. He strongly denied committing these offences, claiming it to be a case of mistaken identity. Then he presented his card, according to which he was formerly employed by China Fresh Egg Co., but admitted

1934 年 7 月 22 日，一位英国女士来到狄思威路捕房报案，称她 5 至 14 岁的子女及其玩伴不敢去虹口公园，因为他们被一名外国人跟踪，此人被认为是葡萄牙人，手臂上搭着一件雨衣，裤子未扣好，向孩子们暴露身体。1934 年 8 月 26 日，上述儿童来到狄思威路捕房陈述，大约在下午 6:30，当他们在公园玩耍时，看到了同一名外国人，坐着并向他们暴露身体。他们要求该男子前往虹口公园门口，那里有警员 84 号迎接他们，并将所有相关人员护送至捕房。在捕房，该外国人自称名为 A.B. Made by D.P.S. Pavloff    Forwarded by C. Gueglio

Valentin Moiseevitch BUIANOVER, Russian, was born
on January 16, 1915 at Vladivostok, Siberia. His late
father was the owner of a shoe store in Vladivostok and
subsequently in Harbin and Shanghai. The applicant left
Vladivostok for Harbin in 1922 together with his parents.
He graduated from a normal school in that city, and in 1929
arrived in Shanghai together with his family. From 1930 to
1931 he was employed with Bills Motors, Fed. Inc. U.S.A.,
Route Cardinal Mercier. Upon leaving this concern, Buianover
and his two brothers established an enterprise of their own
under the name of "Jenny's Service and Auto Supply Co.", at
No.255 Avenue du Roi Albert, which was later removed to No.
177 Rue Amiral Courbet. In April 1938, the applicant sold
his share in the above firm and has since been working for
various companies as a salesman of motor cars.

His brother, L. Buianover has been a member of the
S.M.P. (Specials) since May, 1936.

The applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee and holds passport No.13644 issued on 27-7-37, by
the Police Bureau of the City Government of Shanghai.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to his character.

Date November 19, 1938.

Subject...... Hal P. MILLS - Applicant for enrolment in the Shanghai Municipal
Police (Specials).
Made by.... D. S. Pitts.    Forwarded by....................

Hal Peck MILLS, American, is known as a despicable,
cunning, unprincipled and unscrupulous type of person who
as nominal editor of the "Hwa Mei Chen Pao" and "Hwa Mei
Wan Pao," merely lends his name and nationality for
purposes of protection to a Chinese concern in return for
a monetary remuneration.

Mills' ostensible profession is that of a theatrical
agent and instances have come to light in the past which
have indicated without a shadow of doubt that he has been
guilty of sharp practices towards certain artists passing
through his hands for engagements.

Since he commenced his connection with the newspapers
mentioned above Mills has been warned on several occasions
for having published articles considered either in poor
taste, likely to cause a breach of the peace or definite
falsehoods, but although he has promised to be more care-
ful in future, the warnings he has received have most
blatantly been disregarded.

Although he is known to have been mixed up in many a
shady affair he has always remained on the right side of
the law from a criminal point of view. He has, however,
been thrice convicted in the United States Court for China
for minor breaches of Traffic Regulations.

The applicant is on friendly terms with many members
of this Force but from what is known of him it is believed
that were he able to utilize these acquaintanceships from
a business angle, he would not hesitate to do so.

It is worth pointing out that in many articles he has
had published in the past he has professed great friendship

由.... D. S. Pitts 撰写。    经....................转呈

Hal Peck MILLS，美国人，众所周知是一个卑鄙、狡猾、无原则且肆无忌惮的人，他作为《华美晨报》和《华美晚报》的名义编辑，仅仅为了获取金钱报酬，就将自己的名字和国籍借给一家华商机构以求庇护。

Mills 表面上的职业是戏剧代理人，过去曾发生过一些事件，毫无疑问地表明他对经手安排聘用的某些艺术家存在欺诈行为。

自从他与上述报纸建立联系以来，Mills 曾因发表被认为品味低劣、可能引发治安混乱或明显虚假的文章而多次受到警告，尽管他承诺今后会更加谨慎，但他对这些警告置若罔闻，表现得极为公然。

虽然众所周知他卷入许多可疑事务，但从刑事角度来看，他始终未触犯法律底线。然而，他曾三次在美国在华法院因轻微违反交通法规而被定罪。

申请人与本警队的许多成员关系友好，但根据对其了解，相信如果他能从商业角度利用这些熟人关系，他会毫不犹豫地这样做。

值得指出的是，在他过去发表的许多文章中，他都宣称有着深厚的友谊

Subject Andrew SHIRAZEE - Applicant for enrolment in the Shanghai Municipal
        Police (Specials).
Made by D. S. Pitts.    Forwarded by

Andrew SHIRAZEE, Persian, has been a resident of
Shanghai for many years and is a person of good standing
in the local Parsee community.    Nothing is known to his
detriment from a criminal, moral or political point of view
and from enquiries made he would would most probably
make a suitable recruit for the Municipal Police (Specials).
It is to be noted, though, that he is employed with
the "Hwa Mei Wen Pao," with which Hal P. MILLS is connected,
and should his (Shirazee's) application be approved
and Mills' rejected, the former might find himself
embarrassed from a business point of view, as it is learned
that Mills was responsible for the idea of both men
offering their services to the community, and with the
latter in the position of being nominal head of the
newspaper, Shirazee would, of course be influenced by
any of his actions.

                                        D. S.

Subject Joseph Salem DAVID - Application to join S.M.P. (Specials).

Made by J.S. Henchman Forwarded by C G...

J. S. David, applicant for S.M.P. (Specials), is a British subject, born in Bombay on 17.4.1896. He arrived in Shanghai in 1908, remained for two years, returned to India and then, in 1913, went to the U.S.A. where he resided until 1917. During his sojourn in the U.S.A. he was employed by various insurance companies.

In 1917 David returned to Shanghai and has resided in this town since that date. He has been employed successively with Messrs. Harvy Cook & Co., Calder Marshall & Co. and Manufacturers Life Insurance Co., his present employers.

From 1933 until the present time David has been a member of the S.V.C., but during the whole of that period, except for compulsory mobilisation in 1937, only attended four parades and is, therefore, classed as "inefficient."
(印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL SPECIAL BRANCH 17 1 39)

David's reputation in Shanghai is not of the best, he is addicted to drink and is not considered reliable. During the period of his employment with the firm of Calder Marshall & Co. he was suspected of a series of misappropriations and for this reason was dismissed, clemency on the part of his employers preventing his being prosecuted. His present employers are unaware of his previous delinquences and the above information was given in the strictest confidence.

Though there is nothing in Police records to his detriment, it would not appear that he would make a satisfactory Police Special.

制作人 J.S. Henchman 转呈人 C G...

J. S. David，上海公共租界工部局警务处（特别警察）申请人，系英国臣民，1896年4月17日出生于孟买。他于1908年抵达上海，停留两年后返回印度，随后于1913年前往美国，在那里居住至1917年。在美期间，他曾受雇于多家保险公司。

1917年，戴维返回上海，并自此一直居住于此。他先后受雇于 Harvy Cook & Co. 公司、Calder Marshall & Co. 公司以及 Manufacturers Life Insurance Co.（制造商人寿保险公司），后者为其现任雇主。

从1933年至今，戴维一直是上海万国商团（S.V.C.）的成员，但在整个期间，除1937年的强制动员外，仅参加了四次操练，因此被归类为“不合格”。
(印：上海公共租界工部局特务科 39年1月17日)

戴维在上海的声誉不佳，他有酗酒恶习，被认为不可靠。在 Calder Marshall & Co. 公司任职期间，他涉嫌一系列挪用公款行为，并因此被解雇，因其雇主的宽恕而未遭起诉。他的现任雇主不知晓其之前的过失，上述信息是在严格保密的情况下提供的。

虽然警方档案中没有任何对其不利的记录，但他似乎不会成为一名令人满意的特别警察。

Date January 23, 1939.

Subject Alexander C. Lacson - applicant for appointment in the
Shanghai Municipal Police (Specials).

Made by D.S. Hide Forwarded by C. Crawford

Alexander O. Lacson, who was born in Manila on
May 3, 1891, arrived in Shanghai in 1917 and obtained
employment in the Traffic Department of the Kee Tsong
Tobacco Company. Three years later he joined the staff
of the Standard Oil Company but lost his position on the
reduction of staff in 1924.

On May 18, 1925, he was engaged by Anderson
Meyer & Company Ltd., and posted to their advertising
& Printing Department. He was dismissed for corrupt
practices on December 19, 1931.

The applicant joined the Shanghai Volunteer Corps
in 1927, but resigned during the hostilities in 1932 in
sympathy with his nephew Mr. S.L. Baugista, whose
discharge from the Corps, he considered unjust. He
later rejoined the Corps but was himself dismissed on
September 2, 1938 owing to lack of interest in his duties
and his repeated failure to attend parades and other
functions.

Since it is understood that the foregoing will
debar the applicant's appointment, enquiries regarding
him have been discontinued.

（批：FILE 8/78）

Subject Alfred STEIN - Applicant for enrolment in Shanghai
Municipal Police (Specials)

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by C. ...da ...

Alfred STEIN, German (former Austrian) of Jewish
extraction, was born in Vienna on December 30, 1898.

He first arrived in Shanghai on December 26, 1938
in the s.s. "Jean Laborde," an emigrant endeavouring to
escape the harsh regime imposed by Hitler on all Jews
after the annexation of Austria by the Reich.

The applicant was formerly an officer in the
Austrian Army Reserve and for several years was prominent
in Vienna as an expert on matters relating to the
cultivation of corn and grain.

He is the son-in-law of Mr. A.R. HERTZKA, local
business man who has resided in this city for over twelve
years.

STEIN has opened a business as a manufacturer's
representative at Room 303, 410 Szechuen Road, financial
assistance having been rendered by Mr. HERTZKA. The
applicant, who resides with his wife and ten year old son
at 1809 Avenue Joffre, appears to be an excellent type for
enlistment and may well be in a position to advise in the
near future on the background of other emigrants desirous
of joining the Specials.

Nothing is known by this office to the applicant's
detriment from a criminal, moral or political angle.

阿尔弗雷德·斯坦（Alfred STEIN），德国人（前奥地利人），犹太裔，1898年12月30日出生于维也纳。

他于1938年12月26日首次乘坐“让·拉博德”号（s.s. "Jean Laborde"）轮船抵达上海，是一名试图逃离纳粹德国吞并奥地利后希特勒对所有犹太人实施的严酷政权的移民。

申请人曾是奥地利陆军预备役军官，数年来在维也纳作为玉米和谷物种植方面的专家而闻名。

他是本地商人 A.R. HERTZKA 先生的女婿，赫兹卡先生在本市居住已超过十二年。

斯坦在四川路410号303室开设了一家制造商代表处，资金由赫兹卡先生提供援助。申请人与其妻子及十岁儿子居住在霞飞路1809号，看起来是入伍的优秀人选，并且可能在不久的将来就其他希望加入特别警察的移民的背景提供建议。

本局从刑事、道德或政治角度未发现任何对其不利的记录。

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Campbell A. Q.

John McDonald ELLERY, British, born at Padbury,
Bucks on March 10, 1901, entered the Shanghai Municipal
Police (Gaol) Service on January 22, 1923 and resigned on
January 21, 1938 holding the rank of Senior Warder. His
conduct during this period was officially recorded as
"Excellent."

He left for London in January 1938 in order to
start a business of his own, but owing to the prevalent
general business depression, his commercial venture failed
and he returned to Shanghai in December, 1938.

He secured a post in the Revenue Department of the
S.M.C. in January this year and is at present residing at
55/2 Rue Moliere.

He is known as a steady, industrious and sober
individual against whom nothing of a detrimental nature
is on record.

Sergey Lookianovitch ERMOLAEFF (ERMOLL),
Russian, was born on May 5, 1908 in Harbin. Son
of a former employee of the Chinese Eastern Railway,
he studied in the Harbin Commercial School up to 1923,
after which he proceeded to Shanghai. A musician by
occupation Mr. Ermolaeff has since 1923 been working
in his professional capacity in various cities in
China including Shanghai, Tientsin, Peking, Tsingtao,
Harbin and Dairen and also visited the Netherlands
East Indies in 1928 and 1930. In 1927 he made a trip
to the U.S.A. At present he is the leader of an
orchestra in the "Arcadia Cafe" 291, Rue Amiral
Courbet. Mr. Ermolaeff has a contract with this cafe
which expires on May 1, 1940.

During the course of an interview with the
applicant it was pointed out to him, that one of
the conditions for enlistment in the S.M.P. (Specials)

between 6 p.m. and 12 m.n. during the normal times
and that as his work only starts at 8 or 9 p.m. daily,
he may find it difficult to attend to his duties as a
Special Constable. However, Mr. Ermolaeff, assured the
undersigned that he is in possession of verbal permission
from Mr. Plotnikoff, the owner of the "Arcadia Cafe",
to absent himself on any day should he be required to

Vladimir Zaharovitch MAZUK, Russian, was born
on July 25, 1915, at Blagoveschensk, Siberia. He is
reported to have escaped from the U.S.S.R. in 1928,
together with his mother and to have subsequently
resided in Harbin, Manchuria. Upon graduating from
a local high school in 1932 he proceeded to Chefoo
where he entered the Yih Wen Commercial College.
Upon leaving the College in 1934 he worked as a
mechanic apprentice and a driver in various garages
in that city.

He arrived in Shanghai in December 1937 and
in January 1938, obtained employment with the Texaco
Oil Company in their filling station at 668 Avenue
Foch. In October 1938 he left that concern on his
own accord and in November of the same year became a
co-proprietor of the Popular Service Station, 633
Avenue Foch.

While in Shanghai, he did not come to the
notice of the Municipal Police in connection with
any activities of an undesirable nature.

Made by D.S. Hide Forwarded by C. Crawford.

Stanley Horner-Hoe alias Ho Shie Hwa was
born of Chinese parents in Hongkong on May 19,
1911. He is said to be a relative of Sir Robert
Ho Tung and his father Jackson Hoe was formerly a
chief clerk in the employ of Jardine Matheson &
Co.'s Hongkong Office.

The applicant was educated at St. Pauls
University in Hongkong which he attended from the
age of five to seventeen years. At the age of
eighteen he obtained an appointment as probationary
compradore aboard the Jardine s.s. "Kwaisang" and
was subsequently promoted to second compradore
on the s.s. "Suiwo." He resigned this appointment
in 1933 and secured a position as clerk with the
Shanghai & Hongkew Wharf Co. Ltd., 610 Broadway
East, where he is still employed. His present
superior describe him as industrious, sober and
reliable.

The applicant at present resides at 490
Shanhaikwan Road. Police records contain no
reference to him. He is not a registered British
subject and does not possess a passport.

D.S. Hide

Georg Schoenwald, applicant for enlistment in
the Shanghai Municipal Police (Specials), who was born
in Vienna on September 7, 1892, is a Jewish refugee
who arrived in Shanghai by the s.s. Conte Rosso on
December 31, 1938.

Since February 10, 1939, he has been employed
as a clerk by the Hongkew & Shanghai Wharf Company,
610 Broadway and is held in high esteem by his present
superiors.

The applicant is in possession of the following
documents:-

1. A recommendation from the Union Bank of Vienna
where he was employed from December 1909 until
November 1920.

2. A recommendation from Kirchhelmer & Ehrlick Ltd.
(in liquidation) where he was employed from
October 1920 to April 1929.

3. A recommendation from Hofherr, Schrantz, Clayton
and Shuttleworth by whom he was employed from
July 1929 until September 1938.

4. Certificate of Character No. 8534 issued by the
Vienna Police on August 6, 1938.

5. Passport No. 21633 issued by the Vienna Police.

6. Certificate of Residence issued by the
Vienna Police.

7. Identification Card No. 1765 issued by the
International Committee at Shanghai.

Each of the above recommendations refer to the
applicant as a man of outstanding zeal, character and
ability.

The applicant is at present residing at house 12,
Lane 20 Seymour Road.

Subject. S.V. Poliak , applicant for enlistment in the S.M.P. ( Specials ).
Made by. D. S. Pavloff. Forwarded by. C. Clausen. (签字)
Semen Vulfovitch POLIAK , Russian Jew , was born on March 23 , 1903 at Chita, Siberia. According to his own statement , he left Russia in 1916 and for the following four years resided in Harbin after which he proceeded to Palestine. Returning to Shanghai in 1921 he worked for a short period as a baker in the Chocolate Shop. During 1923 and 1924 he was employed as a porter in the Palace Hotel. From 1924 to 1928 he worked as a supervisor with the Commercial Express and Storage Co., and during 1929 and 1930 with D.G.M. Aranovsky Transport Co. ( now defunct ). In 1932 he secured a position as a supervisor with the International Trucking and Storage Co. , 25 Peking Road. He left that place of employment in the end of 1933 owing to the liquidation of the concern. In 1934 and 1935 he worked as a caretaker with the Probst, Hanbury ( China ) Ltd. , Real Estates Agents , 21 Jinkee Road. This firm went out of existance in the end of 1935. Since April 1936 he has been employed as a supervisor of the night work with the Shanghai & Hongkew Wharf Co. , Ltd.
The applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee , 118/1 Moulmein Road.
While in Shanghai , he did not come to the notice of the Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an undesirable nature.

由 D.S. Pavloff 撰写 经 C. Crawford. J.I 转呈

亚历山大·谢苗诺维奇·涅恰耶夫（Alexander Semenovitch NECHAEFF），俄国人，1918年10月16日出生于俄罗斯滨海省乌苏里斯克（Nikolsk-Ussuryisk）。据报他于1920年随父母离开俄罗斯，随后居住在哈尔滨。1924年，他与姐姐一同从哈尔滨抵达上海。1927年至1930年，他就读于男童公立学校（Public School for Boys），之后在家继续受教育。1934年他前往青岛，并在那里居住至1935年9月，随后返回上海。1936年1月，他在阿尔贝特王路（Avenue du Roi Albert）101号的理查兹汽车行（Richards Auto Works）谋得现职，担任助理机械师。他的哥哥 V.S. Nechaeff 自1937年8月起一直是上海公共租界工部局警务处（特别队）的成员。

申请人已在莫尔美因路（Moulmein Road）118/1号的俄国侨民委员会登记。

工部局警务处档案中没有任何不利于其品行的记录。

REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / S.B. REGISTRY / No. S. B. L. 3867/87 / Date June 27, 39）
Subject Mr. Arthur MAHOMED - applicant to join the Shanghai Municipal
Police (Specials).
Made by D.S. Lockwood Forwarded by W Logan A.S.P.

Mr. Arthur MAHOMED, Portuguese, born in
Macao on March 17, 1904, was educated in the St.
Joseph's College and Escola Commercial, Macao, from
1914-1920, passing the various grades satisfactorily.
On leaving school he joined the Asia Bank, Shameen,
as an assistant book-keeper; he lost this position
in 1922 following the amalgamation of the latter
organization with the International Bank, an American
concern. For the next eleven years, Mr. MAHOMED was
employed as an English and Mathematics teacher in
the Chu-Wei School, Shameen, his services being
terminated prior to the closing of the establishment.
From 1933-1936, MAHOMED continued to live in Shameen,
where he earned a living by acting as a tutor,
specialising in the English language. He arrived in
Shanghai in 1936 and obtained a position as an
Assistant Compradore with the Nippon Yushen Kaisha,
No. 31 The Bund.
There is nothing detrimental to the
character of Mr. MAHOMED known to the Municipal Police.

D. S. Lockwood.
D. S.

D. C. (Special Branch).

由 D.S. Lockwood 撰写 经 W Logan A.S.P. 转呈

Arthur MAHOMED 先生，葡萄牙人，1904年3月17日出生于澳门，1914年至1920年间在澳门圣若瑟修院（St. Joseph's College）和商业学校（Escola Commercial）接受教育，各科成绩合格。离校后，他加入沙面（Shameen）的亚洲银行（Asia Bank）担任助理簿记员；1922年，由于该机构与美国企业国际银行（International Bank）合并，他失去了这一职位。在接下来的十一年里，MAHOMED 先生在沙面的珠维学校（Chu-Wei School）担任英语和数学教师，在该校关闭前终止了服务。1933年至1936年，MAHOMED 继续居住在沙面，通过担任家庭教师谋生，专攻英语教学。他于1936年抵达上海，并在外滩31号的日本邮船会社（Nippon Yushen Kaisha）获得了一份助理买办的职位。
工部局警务处所知范围内，没有任何不利于 MAHOMED 先生品行的记录。

D. S. Lockwood.

Subject F.M. Guterres, applicant to join the S.M. Police (Specials).
Made by. D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Gaspar S.I

Frederick Maria GUTERRES, Portuguese,
born on December 14, 1918 at Shanghai. Upon graduating
from the St. Francis Xavier's College in 1934 he re-
sided with his parents until September, 1937 when he
left for Macao to serve his term of military service
in the Portuguese army. Returning to Shanghai in April,
1939 he was without any fixed employment until August 1,
1939 when he was engaged by the Sumitomo Bank, 69 Kiu-
kiang Road, as a typist and office assistant.

He holds passport No. 32/39 issued by the
Portuguese Consulate-General at Hongkong on 17-4-39.

From March, 1936 to October, 1937 he was
a member of the Portuguese Company, S.V.C. and is well
spoken of by Mr. M.F. Leitao, the company commander.

His father, A.M. Guterres, and his brother,
J.M. Guterres, are employed in the Tea Department of
Dodwell & Co., Ltd, 320 Kiangsi Road, and another bro-
ther of the applicant, A.M. Guterres, is reported to
have been employed with the Sumitomo Bank until recently,
after which he joined the Shanghai Water Works Co.
E.M. Guterres is a Sergeant in the S.M. Police (Specials).

Nothing detrimental is known in this office
regarding the applicant.

A. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

A. C. ( Special Branch ).

Frederick Maria GUTERRES，葡萄牙人，1918年12月14日出生于上海。1934年从圣方济各沙勿略学院（St. Francis Xavier's College）毕业后，他与父母同住，直到1937年9月前往澳门，在葡萄牙军队中服兵役。1939年4月返回上海后，他一直处于无固定职业状态，直到1939年8月1日被九江路69号的住友银行（Sumitomo Bank）聘为打字员和办公室助理。

他持有香港葡萄牙总领事馆于1939年4月17日签发的第32/39号护照。

1936年3月至1937年10月期间，他是上海万国商团（S.V.C.）葡萄牙连队的成员，并受到连长 M.F. Leitao 先生的好评。

他的父亲 A.M. Guterres 和兄弟 J.M. Guterres 受雇于江西路320号的德和洋行（Dodwell & Co., Ltd）茶叶部，申请人的另一位兄弟 A.M. Guterres 据报最近一直在住友银行工作，之后加入了上海自来水公司（Shanghai Water Works Co.）。E.M. Guterres 是上海公共租界工部局警务处（特别队）的一名警佐。

1. Hans Georg ALGUTIER, German of Jewish origin, born on May 21, 1910 at Beuten, Upper Silesia, Germany. He holds passport No. B - 24 issued on September 2, 1935 by the police authorities at Beuten. "Victoria".
In Shanghai he has been employed with Bennet Freres, Hamilton House, since November, 1938. He resides at 1094 Avenue Road together with his junior brother, L.G. Algutier, 25, who is reported to have arrived in Shanghai from Germany about two years ago and is at present employed with the Chinese Rolling Aluminium Mills, Ltd., 610 Weichow Road.

2. Hans HIRSCH, German of Jewish origin, born on February 10, 1914 at Ravitsch, Germany. He holds passport No. H.- 98/37 issued by the Breslau Police on 22-2-37. According to his own statement, his late father was a merchant in Breslau and his mother at present resides in Columbia, South America.
Hirsch left Germany in December, 1938 for Italy where he embarked the s.s. "Potsdam" bound for the Far East and on 31-12-39 arrived in Shanghai. Here he claims to have been working as a salesman for various firms for some time and at present to be employed as

由 J. S. I. Prokofiev 撰写    经 C. Crawford 转呈。

1. Hans Georg ALGUTIER，犹太裔德国人，1910年5月21日出生于德国上西里西亚的博伊滕（Beuten）。他持有博伊滕警察当局于1935年9月2日签发的 B - 24 号护照。从该护照看来，他的职业是商行职员，且于1938年6月11日离开德国前往意大利，随后从该国前往远东，于1938年9月11日乘坐“维多利亚”号轮船（s.s. "Victoria"）抵达本市。
在上海，他自1938年11月以来一直受雇于汉密尔顿大厦（Hamilton House）的 Bennet Freres 公司。他与25岁的弟弟 L.G. Algutier 同住于爱文义路（Avenue Road）1094号，据报其弟约两年前从德国抵达上海，目前受雇于魏州路（Weichow Road）610号的中国轧铝厂有限公司（Chinese Rolling Aluminium Mills, Ltd.）。

2. Hans HIRSCH，犹太裔德国人，1914年2月10日出生于德国的拉维茨（Ravitsch）。他持有布雷斯劳（Breslau）警察局于1937年2月22日签发的 H.- 98/37 号护照。据他自己陈述，他已故的父亲是布雷斯劳的商人，母亲目前居住在南美洲的哥伦比亚（Columbia）。
Hirsch 于1938年12月离开德国前往意大利，在那里登上开往远东的“波茨坦”号轮船（s.s. "Potsdam"），并于1939年12月31日抵达上海。（注：原文日期疑似有误，结合上下文应为1938年底或1939年初抵达，但此处照实翻译原文）在此，他声称一段时间以来一直为多家公司担任推销员，目前受雇于

Subject M.Marcus, H. Socholler and K. Socholler - candidates to join the
S.M.P. ( Specials ).

Made by. D.S.I. Prokofiev.    Forwarded by R W. Mac Aulie D S I

1. Martin MARCUS, German citizen of Jewish ori-
gin, born on June 4,1906 at Berlin. He holds passport
No. II/4589/38 issued by the Berlin Police on 10-11-38.
A merchant by occupation, he left Germany for the Far
East on 19-12-38 aboard the s.s. "Gneisenau" and arrived
in Shanghai on 27-1-39. Here he resided at 34 Studley
Avenue until about two months ago when he removed to his
present address, 1094 Avenue Road ( Henley House ).
In May, 1939 he established a small business at 668 Sze-
chuen Road known as "Elite Fashion Company", Manufactu-
rers of Ladies Blouses and Dresses, which he has since
been conducting together with his father, Mr. Samuel
Marcus, merchant, who arrived in Shanghai together with
him.

2. Karl SOCHOLLER, German citizen of Jewish ori-
gin, born on December 17, 1911 at Vienna. He is reported
to have left Vienna for Italy in November, 1938 and later
to have proceeded to the Far East arriving in this city
on 20-12-38 in the s.s. "Conte Biancamano". From the be-
ginning of 1939 he has been residing at House 49 Hwa Kee
Avenue, 1025 Bubbling Well Road and since May, 1939 is
reported to have been employed with Reiss, Bradley & Co.,
Ltd, 210 Szechuen Road, as a salesman on a fixed salary
plus commission.

He holds passport No 16326 issued by the Vien-
na Police on 1-9-38 and a certificate of character issued
by the same authorities on 9-5-38 in connection with his
intention to apply for a visa to enter Australia.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 1939）
（批：Fund 26/10）

1. Martin MARCUS，犹太裔德国公民，1906年6月4日出生于柏林。他持有柏林警察局于1938年11月10日签发的 II/4589/38 号护照。职业为商人，他于1938年12月19日乘坐“格奈森瑙”号轮船（s.s. "Gneisenau"）离开德国前往远东，并于1939年1月27日抵达上海。在此，他居住在斯塔德利路（Studley Avenue）34号，直到大约两个月前搬至现址爱文义路（Avenue Road）1094号（亨利公寓 Henley House）。1939年5月，他在四川路668号创办了一家名为“精英时装公司”（Elite Fashion Company）的小型企业，制造女士衬衫和连衣裙，此后他一直与父亲 Samuel Marcus 先生（商人，与他一同抵达上海）共同经营该公司。

2. Karl SOCHOLLER，犹太裔德国公民，1911年12月17日出生于维也纳。据报他于1938年11月离开维也纳前往意大利，随后前往远东，于1938年12月20日乘坐“比安卡马诺伯爵”号轮船（s.s. "Conte Biancamano"）抵达本市。自1939年初以来，他一直居住在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）1025号华琪路（Hwa Kee Avenue）49号寓所，据报自1939年5月以来，他受雇于四川路210号的 Reiss, Bradley & Co., Ltd 公司，担任固定薪金加佣金的推销员。

他持有维也纳警察局于1938年9月1日签发的第16326号护照，以及同一当局于1938年5月9日出具的品行证明书，该证明与其申请进入澳大利亚的签证意向有关。

Rudolf Arthur NEUMANN, German Jew, was born on
July 25, 1899, in Hamburg, Germany. This applicant
emigrated from Germany together with his wife in May
1939, arriving in this port on June 2, 1939 in the s.s.

Subject. B.A. Dubrovo. Applicant for enlistment in the S.M.P. (Specials).

Made by. D.S. Pavloff Forwarded by. D.L. Crawford.

Boris Abramovitch DUBROVO, Russian Jew, was born
on March 17, 1910 in Novonikolaevsk, Siberia. Accord-
ing to his own statement he left Russia together with
his parents in 1917 and subsequently resided in Harbin.
In 1929 he left Harbin for Likden, where he was employed
by the Harbin Fur Corporation. In 1930 he was trans-
ferred to Tientsin and worked for the same company until
1935. During the same year he started a business, United
Transporters in company with one, E.L. Vinogradoff. After
the occupation of Tientsin by the Japanese forces and the
inauguration of the Anti-Communists Committee in that
city, the applicant applied to the Soviet Consulate in
Tientsin for Soviet papers and was issued with a receipt
to that effect. He resided in Tientsin on the strength
of that receipt, being exempt from registration with the
Anti-Communists Committee. However, early in 1939 he was
obliged to close his business and proceeded to Shanghai.
In May 1939 he started the same business in Shanghai with
an office at Room 405, 113 Kiukiang Road. In May 1939
the applicant visited the local Soviet Consulate with the
object of obtaining his passport. According to his own
statement, he was not given one and was told to wait until
the papers would arrive from Moscow. It is not known
whether the applicant is in possession of a Soviet pass-
port at present or not.

He is not registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee or any other Russian public organization.

鲍里斯·阿布拉莫维奇·杜布罗沃（Boris Abramovitch DUBROVO），俄罗斯犹太人，1910年3月17日出生于西伯利亚新尼古拉耶夫斯克（Novonikolaevsk）。据其自述，他于1917年随父母离开俄国，随后居住在哈尔滨。1929年，他离开哈尔滨前往利克登（Likden，音译），受雇于哈尔滨皮草公司。1930年，他被调往天津，并在同一家公司工作至1935年。同年，他与一名叫 E.L. Vinogradoff 的人合伙创办了“联合运输行”（United Transporters）。在日军占领天津并成立该市的反共委员会后，申请人向苏联驻天津领事馆申请苏联证件，并获得了一张以此为目的的收据。他凭此收据居住在天津，免于在反共委员会登记。然而，1939年初，他被迫关闭业务并前往上海。1939年5月，他在上海重操旧业，办公地点位于九江路113号405室。1939年5月，申请人访问了当地苏联领事馆，旨在获取护照。据其自述，他未获发护照，并被告知需等待文件从莫斯科寄达。目前尚不清楚申请人是否持有苏联护照。

他未在俄侨委员会或任何其他俄罗斯公共组织注册。

Valentin HERPER, German Jewish refugee, arrived
in Shanghai from Europe on June 4, 1939 in the s.s.
"Usaramo". Born in Polizin, Germany on April 24, 1880,
the applicant is an architect by profession. He is
in possession of a fair amount of money and is
residing at 207 Route Winling where he also has an
office whence he practices his business as an architect.
Nothing is known to the applicants detriment
by this office. He fought on the side of the Central
Powers during the Great War and is fully conversant
with the use of military weapons and military
discipline. In the list of qualifications for
enrolment in the Specials, however, it is laid down
that the successful recruit must be able to speak
and understand English. Mr. Herper's knowledge of
English is practically nil but he is undergoing a
course of instruction in this tongue and it would seem
advisable if he re-applied for enrolment in another
three months' time when he will have had the
opportunity of improving his knowledge of the required
language.

Dwyer Augustus NEVILLE, British, was born on
a British ship off Singapore in 1892.
He has spent a number of years in the Far East
and came to Shanghai in June 1938 from Harbin where
he was in the insurance business. On arrival in
Shanghai he became a professional photographer and
took a partnership in the World News Photos Company,
635 Szechuen Road. He is engaged in this business

Neville was attached to the Royal Air Force
during the last World War and is a member of the
Royal Air Force Club in Shanghai. He speaks fluent
Russian and Japanese and a little German.
He is not the subject of any reports in the
records of the Municipal Police and nothing is known
to his detriment.

事由. JOAOZINHO FERDINANDO COLLACO，申请在上海公共租界工部局警务处（特别队）任职。

制作人. D.S.I. Hide, 转呈人 D.I. Crawford.

（批：抄送 C.C (特别队)）

若昂齐尼奥·费尔南多·科拉科（Joaozinho Ferdinando Collaco），申请在上海公共租界工部局警务处（特别队）任职，居住在豫园路1076/5号，是 J.O. 科拉科先生（受雇于九江路20号的莱斯特、约翰逊与莫里斯公司（Lester, Johnson & Morris），担任主管）的儿子，其妻子已于数年前去世。

1930年在圣方济各沙勿略学院完成学业后，申请人加入了汇丰银行（Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation）的职员队伍，但其表现不尽如人意，一年后辞职。直到1935年，他才再次获得固定工作，被丽都游泳池（Lido Swimming Pool）聘为管理员和救生员。1937年初，他加入澳门的葡萄牙军队，服役十四个月后，在澳门自来水公司找到了一份工作。

1938年4月，他返回上海，在莱斯特、约翰逊与莫里斯公司担任主管，至今仍受雇于此。

申请人会说英语、葡萄牙语和上海话，以及少许粤语和普通话。
警务处档案中没有关于他的记录，调查也未发现任何不利于他的情况。

他持有在香港签发的葡萄牙护照，编号为 9/B9。

Subject Rudolf R. GLASER - Applicant for enrolment in S.M.P. (Specials).

Made by... D.S. Pitts Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

Rudolf R. GLASER, German Jewish refugee, born in Berlin
on October 8, 1910, arrived in Shanghai from Europe on
November 12, 1938.

He has been conducting an Insurance agency at 103
Kiukiang Road for several months and his efforts have met
with a certain amount of financial success.

Due to the fact that he is of German nationality, the
applicant, a former member of the French Police Specials,
has been informed that his services are no longer required
by this organization.

GLASER is able to speak English well but he is of the
type that is not amenable to discipline. Nothing is known
to his detriment but from contact with him by members of this
office he does not appear to be a suitable candidate for the
S.M.P. (Specials).

REPORT
Subject Kurt HAIN - Applicant for enrolment in the S.M.P. (Specials).
Made by. D.S. Pitts, Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.
Kurt HAIN, Austrian Jewish refugee, who
arrived in Shanghai from Europe on June 20, 1939
in the s.s. "Hashimi Maru," was born in Vienna on
March 27, 1914.
He speaks excellent English and for the
past 2½ months has been employed in a small position
with the General Electric Company, Ningpo Road.
Prior to that he was with the Radio-Technical
Industries, Route Say Zoong.
He is spoken of in refugee circles as a
quiet, clean living person with plenty of common
sense. He is reputed to have been a fine athlete
in Austria. He has no previous military training
of any kind, however.
Since he has been in Shanghai for less than
a year, it would be advisable if he were informed
to make a further application in say, six months
time, when this office would be better enabled to
judge the true merits of the case.
HAIN'S present address is 65 Route Mayen.

呈报人：D.S. 皮茨（Pitts），转呈人：D.I. 克劳福德（Crawford）。
库尔特·海恩，奥地利犹太难民，于1939年6月20日乘“Hashimi Maru”号轮船从欧洲抵达上海，1914年3月27日出生于维也纳。
他英语流利，在过去两个半月里受雇于宁波路通用电气公司（General Electric Company），担任低级职员。在此之前，他就职于霞飞路（Route Say Zoong）的无线电技术工业公司（Radio-Technical Industries）。
在难民圈中，他被描述为一个安静、生活检点且极具常识的人。据称他在奥地利时是一名优秀的运动员。然而，他此前没有任何形式的军事训练经历。
鉴于他抵沪不足一年，建议通知其在六个月左右再次提出申请，届时本处将能更好地评估该案件的实际优劣。
海恩目前的住址是迈恩路（Route Mayen）65号。

(Specials)
Made by. D.S. Hitta Forwarded by. D.I. Crawford

(批：Copy to D.C.(Specials))

Ernst SALOMON, German Jewish refugee, who
arrived in Shanghai from Europe on December 31,
1938 in the s.s. "Conte Rosso", was born in
Dresden on May 28, 1920.

He speaks good English and as far as can
be ascertained is of good character, although
he is believed not to be amenable to discipline.
He has filed an application to join the River
Police but it has not yet been entertained.

He works for his father, Max SALOMON, 138
Hamilton House, who buys and sells sewing-machines,
radios, and other mechanical contrivances.

Article 5 of the qualifications for re-
cruiting in the S.M.P. (Specials) stipulates
that candidates must be at least 21 years of age.
SALOMON is not yet 20 and it would be preferable
if he reapplied in another year's time.

(签名)
D. S.

D.C. (Special Branch)

恩斯特·萨洛蒙，德国犹太难民，于1938年12月31日乘“Conte Rosso”号轮船从欧洲抵达上海，1920年5月28日出生于德累斯顿。
他英语良好，据查品行端正，尽管被认为不太服从纪律。他曾提交加入水上警察队的申请，但尚未被受理。

REPORT

Subject Y.G. Hramchenko, applicant for enlistment in the S.M.P.(Special).

Made by D. S. Pavloff Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

Yakov Grigorievitch Hramchenko, Russian Jew,
was born on February 2, 1909 in Harbin, Manchuria.
Since 1924 he worked first as an apprentice and later
as an assistant pharmacist in various drug stores
in Harbin. In 1927 he secured a diploma of a phar-
macist and continued working in his professional
capacity.
In 1931 he arrived in Shanghai from Harbin
and here again worked in his professional capacity
until August 12, 1940 when he secured his present
position as a salesman with the Medical Section of
the Jardine, Matheson & Co. Ltd.
Whilst in Harbin this applicant possessed a
Soviet passport, however, upon arrival in Shanghai
he denounced his allegiance to the Soviet Government
and is now registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, as a Russian Emigrant.
There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records detrimental to his character.

D. C. (Special Branch).

（批：D. S.）

雅科夫·格里戈里耶维奇·赫拉姆琴科（Yakov Grigorievitch Hramchenko），俄罗斯犹太人，1909年2月2日出生于满洲哈尔滨。自1924年起，他先在哈尔滨各家药店当学徒，后担任助理药剂师。1927年，他获得药剂师文凭，并继续从事本专业工作。
1931年，他从哈尔滨抵达上海，在此继续从事本专业工作，直到1940年8月12日，他在怡和洋行有限公司（Jardine, Matheson & Co. Ltd.）医药部谋得现任销售员职位。

Subject G.H. Santos, applicant for enlistment in the S.M.P. (Specials).

Made by D. S. Pavloff Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

George Henry SANTOS, Fillipino, was born on
October 23, 1920 in Vladivostok, Maritime Province,
Russia. According to his own statement, his father,
Leon Santos, Fillipino resided in Vladivostok since 1918
and was employed as a croupier in some gambling
establishment in that city. It was during that time
that he met a certain Russian lady named, Solgarina,
whom, according to the applicant's statement, he
officially married.

The applicant arrived in Shanghai from
Vladivostok, together with his parents in 1926. In
1929 he entered the St. Francis Xavier's College in
which he studied up to 1938.

In January 1938 he obtained a position as a
fitter with the Henningsen Produce Company, where he
is still employed.

He is not in the possession of a passport of
any description and is not registered with either
American Consulate or the Russian Emigrants' Committee.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records detrimental to his character.

(1). Jose MENDOZA,Filipino,was born on Febru-
ary 20,1909 at Shanghai. He attended the St.Fransis Xa-
vier's College until 1924, after which he was employed
as a clerk in the Shanghai Electric Construction Co.,Ltd
from 1925 to 1927. For the past ten years or so he has
been employed in a similar capacity with Messrs Calder-
Marshall & Co,Ltd, 2 Peking Road.
He is registered with the local American
Consulate-General as a Filipino citizen since April,1930
and holds a certificate issued by that Consulate on
14-7-31 in lieu of passport for travelling to Manila.
At present he resides at 15/6 Carter Road together with
his wife and child.
From 1931 to 1940 he was a member of the Fi-
lipino Company,S.V.C.
(2). James MENDOZA,Filipino, was born on Novem-
ber 5,1920 at Shanghai and is the nephew of Jose Mendoza
referred to above. From 1928 to 1936 he attended the
St. Francis Xavier's College,after which he was unemployed
until June,1940 when he obtained his present position of
a proof-reader in the "China Press".
Being under age,he has neither a passport
nor a certificate of nationality. His father is reported
to be at present employed as a supervisor with Henningsen
Produce Company in their factory ,Dawgin Road.
From 5-5-39 to 28-6-40 he was a member of
the Filipino Company, S.V.C.
At present he resides at 15/6 Carter Road.

(1). 何塞·门多萨（Jose MENDOZA），菲律宾人，1909年2月20日出生于上海。他就读于圣方济各沙勿略学院直至1924年，随后于1925年至1927年间受雇于上海电力建设有限公司（Shanghai Electric Construction Co.,Ltd）担任职员。在过去十年左右的时间里，他在北京路2号的考尔德-马歇尔有限公司（Messrs Calder-Marshall & Co,Ltd）担任类似职务。
自1930年4月起，他在当地美国总领事馆注册为菲律宾公民，并持有该领事馆于1931年7月14日签发的证书，以代替前往马尼拉的护照。目前，他与妻子和孩子同住于卡特路（Carter Road）15/6号。
1931年至1940年间，他是上海志愿团（S.V.C.）菲律宾连的成员。
(2). 詹姆斯·门多萨（James MENDOZA），菲律宾人，1920年11月5日出生于上海，是上述何塞·门多萨的侄子。1928年至1936年，他就读于圣方济各沙勿略学院，此后一直失业，直到1940年6月在《字林西报》（China Press）获得现任校对员职位。
因未成年，他既无护照也无国籍证明。据报其父目前在道金路（Dawgin Road）的亨宁森农产品公司工厂担任监工。
1939年5月5日至1940年6月28日，他是上海志愿团（S.V.C.）菲律宾连的成员。
目前，他居住于卡特路（Carter Road）15/6号。

(3) Alexander Evgenievich SHIMANOVSKY, Russian,
was born on August 8, 1910 at Irkutsk, Siberia. He is re-
ported to have left Russia for Manchuria in 1920 and for
the following 18 years to have resided mainly in Harbin.
In 1929 he graduated from the First Russian Private Middle
School in that city, after which he attended the Harbin Po-
lytechnic Institute for over one year. According to his
own statement, he later completed a correspondence course
in Radio-Engineering at the Lincoln Engineering School,
U.S.A.

Since June, 1938 he has been residing in Shang-
hai. Here he conducted a radio-engineering school at 147
Route de Say Zoong from 1938 to June, 1940 and also radio-
engineering classes at the Y.M.C.A., 150 Bubbling Well Road
from 1939 to 1940. From April, 1939 to July, 1940 he is
reported to have been a partner in the Radio & Electric
Industries, 145 Route de Say Zoong, following which he work-
ed casually with Westinghouse Electric Refrigerators &
Appliances, 620 Szechuen Road, as a salesman on a commis-
sion basis. On 1-10-40 he established his own business
under the style " Commercial Brokerage Co", at 110 Szechun
en Road, Room 59 ( Tel. 15804 ).

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants Com-
mittee, Moulmein Road, and at present resides at 343 Route
Cardinal Mercier together with his wife and child.

自1938年6月以来，他一直居住在上海。在此期间，他于1938年至1940年6月在霞飞路（Route de Say Zoong）147号开办了一所无线电工程学校，并于1939年至1940年在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）150号的青年会（Y.M.C.A.）开设无线电工程课程。据报，1939年4月至1940年7月，他是霞飞路145号无线电与电气工业公司（Radio & Electric Industries）的合伙人，此后他在四川路620号的西屋电气冰箱与电器公司（Westinghouse Electric Refrigerators & Appliances）做临时推销员，按佣金计酬。1940年10月1日，他在四川路110号59室（电话 15804）以自己的名义成立了“商业经纪行”（Commercial Brokerage Co）。

Naum Ezekilevitch GLOOS, Russian Jew, was
born on September 18, 1911 in Vladivostok, Maritime
Province, Russia. He is reported to have escaped from
U.S.S.R. to Manchuria in 1931 together with his father
and to have subsequently resided in Harbin. In
December 1931 he arrived in Shanghai from Harbin
together with his father. In 1932 they established
a business of their own under the style, M. I. Gloos,
Painting Contractors, 814 Avenue Joffre. Since his
father's death in October 1939, the applicant has been
a sole proprietor of the same business.

This applicant is registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Route Pichon.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records detrimental to his character.

German Jewish refugee, who arrived in Shanghai on
January 15, 1939 1940. He is in possession of German "J"
passport, II/3693-38, issued in Berlin, October 14, 1938.
KASSTAN, on December 16, 1939, was the
recipient of a letter from the Commissioner of Police,
thanking him for effecting the arrest of a male
Chinese, who had snatched a hand-bag from a female on
Bubbling Well Road on December 14 (B.W. F.I.R.3199/39).

to the detriment of this man's character. People in
the town with whom he has been connected have stated
that he is of a conscientious nature, keen and likely
to make a good special constable.

local Jewish newspaper, the Jewish Chronicle.

Victor Valentinovich [Maklaeff], Russian emigrant,

Province of Russia.
He arrived in Manchuria from Russia with his
parents in 1920.
He received his education at the Y.M.C.A. School

here he joined the Russian Detachment, S.V.C.

remained with this firm until January 1st., 1940.

Heningsen Produce Coy., at 450 Swaygin Road and is still

maker.

Victor Valentinovich [Maklaeff]，俄国流亡者，
1919 年 1 月 30 日出生于俄罗斯外贝加尔省赤塔。
他于 1920 年随父母从俄罗斯抵达满洲。
他在哈尔滨基督教青年会学校接受教育，并于 1937 年毕业。
毕业后不久，他随父母离开哈尔滨前往上海。抵达此处后，他加入了上海义勇队（S.V.C.）俄籍分队。
他在该分队服役至 1938 年底，随后辞职加入四川北路 668 号的 Hongay Sales Corporation（音译）担任主管，并一直在此公司工作至 1940 年 1 月 1 日。
他辞去该公司职务，加入绥远路 450 号的 Heningsen Produce Coy.（亨宁森食品公司），目前仍在该公司担任糖果制作工。

Made by. J.D.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

(Copy forwarded to Registry)

PERSONAL ASSISTANT
20 NOV.
To Deputy Commissioner (Crime)

Valentin Ivanovich GREMKIN, Russian, born on February 16, 1918 at Nikolaevsk-on-Amur, Siberia. Reported to be the son of a Russian officer who was killed by the Bolsheviks in 1920, he arrived in Shanghai from Vladivostok via Tsingtao in 1924 together with his mother, Mrs. Nathalie V. Gremkin. From 1924 to 1927 he is reported to have attended the Thomas Hanbury School and from 1929 to 1937 - the Commercial School of the Russian Orthodox Confraternity. Upon graduating from the latter school he was employed with the Shanghai Dollar Directory as a clerk and canvassing agent for about four months ( 1937-1938 ). In November, 1938 he joined the Henningsen Produce Company as an apprentice candy-maker and is still employed with that company.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants Committee and the French Police ( Reg. No. 1697 of 15-2-38 ) and at present resides at 590 Foch Road, house 70, Room 7 together with his mother.

While in Shanghai he did not come to Police notice.

A. Prokofiev.

Gremkin 夫人从符拉迪沃斯托克经青岛抵达上海。据报他于 1924 年至 1927 年就读于汉璧礼西童公学，1929 年至 1937 年就读于俄罗斯东正教兄弟会商业学校。从后者学校毕业后，他在《上海美元名录》担任职员和推销员约四个月（1937-1938 年）。1938 年 11 月，他作为学徒糖果工加入 Henningsen Produce Company（亨宁森食品公司），目前仍受雇于该公司。

Alexander Alexandrovich Almod, Latvian citizen,
single, was born on December 1st., 1914 in Harbin.
His father was formerly employed by the Chinese
Maritime Customs in North China.
He received his education at the Russian
Commercial School and at the Russian College in Harbin
but left the latter, in 1931, before graduating.
He left Harbin for Shanghai at the beginning of 1932
and upon his arrival here he entered the Public Thomas
Hanbury School from which he graduated in 1935.
Between 1935 and 1937 he also attended the Russian
Business College in Shanghai.
In 1939 he was for a short duration employed at
the Asia Construction Coy in the capacity of a book-
keeper and at the E. Merck Chemical Coy as a stock keeper
and left this company in May 1940.
Following his resignation from the E. Merck
Chemical Coy he obtained the position of an assistant
superintendant of the Service Station Dept. with the
Texas Co. (China ) Ltd., where he is still employed.
There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to the applicant's character.

Alexander Alexandrovich Almod，拉脱维亚公民，
单身，1914 年 12 月 1 日出生于哈尔滨。
其父此前曾受雇于华北的中国海关。
他在哈尔滨的俄罗斯商业学校和俄罗斯学院接受教育，但于 1931 年在毕业前离开了后者。

With reference to the attached application
for enrolment in the S.M.P. (Specials), the applicant,
Fred S. COHEN, who is also known as Siegfried COHN,
is a German Jew, born in Memel on January 9, 1913.
He is in possession of German "J" passport, No. 235/38,
issued by the German Consulate General in Shanghai,
on August 5, 1938.
Cohen arrived in Shanghai on August 9, 1936
but after two years left for Hong Kong, as he wished
to apply for British naturalisation. He was interned
for a period of five weeks on the outbreak of the
European war and returned to Shanghai on October 15,
1939.
He joined the Jewish Company, S.V.C. but
only served for fourteen days during the local hostilities
in August, 1937.
Cohen is at present employed by the Pacific
American Trading Company, 80 Szechuen Road, and has been
in this employ for the past two years. His employers
are satisfied with his services and state that he has
so far proved conscientious and willing. Previous to
leaving for Hong Kong, Cohen was employed by his father-
in - law, Mr. R. DEITCH, manager of the British Manufac-
turing Company, 795 Bubbling Well Road, who is himself
a naturalised British subject.
Whilst there is nothing to the detriment of
the applicant on file at Police Headquarters, his
general demeanour did not leave a very favourable
impression and it is doubtful whether Cohen is of the

关于所附加入上海公共租界警务处（特别队）的申请，申请人 Fred S. COHEN，又名 Siegfried COHN，是一名德籍犹太人，1913 年 1 月 9 日出生于梅梅尔。他持有德国“J”字护照，编号 235/38，由德国驻上海总领事馆于 1938 年 8 月 5 日签发。
Cohen 于 1936 年 8 月 9 日抵达上海，但两年后前往香港，因为他希望申请英国归化。欧洲战争爆发时，他被拘禁了五周，并于 1939 年 10 月 15 日返回上海。
他加入了上海义勇队（S.V.C.）犹太连，但在 1937 年 8 月的本地战事期间仅服役了十四天。
Cohen 目前受雇于四川北路 80 号的太平洋美国贸易公司，并已在此工作两年。其雇主对他的服务表示满意，并称他迄今为止表现出认真负责和乐于工作的态度。在前往香港之前，Cohen 曾受雇于其岳父 R. DEITCH 先生，后者是静安寺路 795 号英国制造公司的经理，其本人已是归化的英国臣民。

Alexey Vassili vich STEPENSKY ( Stepensky ),
Russian, born on July 5, 1903 at Arch, South Russia. He
is reported to have arrived in Shanghai from Vladivostok
in or about 1920. From 1920 to 1924 he attended the
St. Francis Xavier's College, after leaving which he is
reported to have been employed in the British American
Tobacco Company in 1925-1926. In 1927 he joined the
Russian Detachment of Marshal Chang Chung Chang's Army
in Shantung, in which he served until some time in 1928.
Returning to Shanghai, he joined the Russian Detachment,
S.V.C., on 8-5-28. On 31-7-29 he left this service of his
own accord and for the following ten years was employed
with the British American Tobacco Company ( at present
known as Tse Soong Tobacco Company ) as a foreman. He
left this service on 30-10-40 and is in possession of a
good testimonial from the firm. At present he conducts
his own business - Alexida Co., ( Suit & Overcoat Lengths)
at 778 Bubbling Well Road, Flat 54 ( Denis Apartments ).
He is registered with the Russian Emigrants
Committee, Moulmein Road, and resides at the above ad-
dress together with his wife, Mrs Ida M. Stzepensky, 37.
He is the holder of S.M.P. licence No. 2082
for carrying arms ( issued on 11-1-38 ).
The only time he came to Police notice was
in May, 1929, when he was a member of the Russian Regiment,
S.V.C. It appears that on 7-5-29, being under the influ-
ence of drink, and armed with a revolver, the property of
the S.V.C., he was apprehended by the Chinese Police in

阿列克谢·瓦西里耶维奇·斯捷彭斯基（Alexey Vassili vich STEPENSKY，亦作 Stepensky），
俄罗斯人，1903 年 7 月 5 日出生于南俄阿尔汉格尔斯克（Arch）。据报他于 1920 年左右从符拉迪沃斯托克抵达上海。1920 年至 1924 年，他就读于圣方济各沙勿略学院（St. Francis Xavier's College），离校后据报于 1925-1926 年间受雇于英美烟草公司。1927 年，他加入张宗昌元帅在山东的军队中的俄罗斯分队，服役至 1928 年的某个时候。返回上海后，他于 1928 年 5 月 8 日加入上海义勇队（S.V.C.）俄罗斯分队。1929 年 7 月 31 日，他自愿离职，并在随后的十年间受雇于英美烟草公司（现称“子松烟草公司” Tse Soong Tobacco Company）担任领班。他于 1940 年 10 月 30 日离职，并持有该公司出具的良好推荐信。目前他经营自己的生意——Alexida 公司（西装及大衣面料），地址为静安寺路 778 号德义公寓（Denis Apartments）54 室。

他在摩尔门路（Moulmein Road）的俄罗斯侨民委员会登记注册，并与妻子伊达·M·斯捷彭斯基夫人（Mrs Ida M. Stzepensky，37 岁）居住于上述地址。

他持有上海公共租界警务处颁发的第 2082 号持枪许可证（签发于 1938 年 1 月 11 日）。

他唯一一次引起警方注意是在 1929 年 5 月，当时他是上海义勇队（S.V.C.）俄罗斯团的一员。看来在 1929 年 5 月 7 日，他在醉酒状态下，携带一支属于上海义勇队的左轮手枪，被华捕逮捕于

Charles Tyau Yee ONM is a British Malayan
subject born on November 10, 1919 at Ipoh, Malaya.
His father is a Chinese Malayan and his mother a
Portugese. Until March 1939, applicant worked as
a clerk for his father who owns a tin mine in Ipoh,
in March however, he proceeded to Saigon where, for
1½ years he was employed as a clerk by the Standard
Vacuum Oil Co. In September 1940 he resigned from

Date Feb. 12th 1941
Subject Anatoly Valerianovich Ilioff - applicant for enlistment in
the Shanghai Municipal Police ( Specials ).
Made by C.D.I. Maclaevsky Forwarded by C.D.I. Paorun.

Anatoly Valerianovich Ilioff, Russian subject,
married, of Greek-Orthodox Religion, was born on June 12th.
1903 in Tsitsikar, Manchuria. His father was formerly
employed with the North Manchurian Railway. In 1906
the applicant left Manchuria for Khabarovsk, Russia
together with his parents. The applicant entered a
River Navigation School in Khabarovsk from which he
graduated in 1918 as a qualified ship's mechanic. Since
then he was serving on various river boats plying on
Amur River.

In 1922 when Khabarovsk was occupied by White
Russian Army he enlisted in the Russian Navy and was
assigned to a warship which was stationed in Kamchatka
Bay. In 1923 following the collapse of the White Russian
Government in the Russian Far East, Russian Fleet sailed
for Manila where he was discharged in 1924. In the same
year he left Manila for Harbin and shortly afterwards he
joined the White Russian Detachment serving the Chinese
Army of Marshal Chang Tso Ling, War Lord of Manchuria.
He served with this Detachment until 1927 when, upon his
discharge, left for Shanghai. In August 1927 he obtained
the position of an assistant engineer with the Shanghai
Waterworks Company and remained with this Company until
November 1940 when he resigned of his own accord.

由刑事侦缉督察马卡耶夫斯基（Maclaevsky）呈报，经刑事侦缉督察鲍伦（Paorun）转呈。

阿纳托利·瓦列里安诺维奇·伊利奥夫，俄国籍，已婚，希腊正教徒，1903年6月12日出生于满洲齐齐哈尔。其父曾受雇于北满铁路。1906年，申请人随父母离开满洲前往俄国哈巴罗夫斯克。申请人进入哈巴罗夫斯克的一所内河航运学校学习，并于1918年毕业，取得合格船舶机械师资格。此后，他在航行于黑龙江上的各类内河船只上服役。

1922年，当哈巴罗夫斯克被俄国白军占领时，他加入俄国海军，并被派往一艘驻泊在堪察加湾的军舰上服役。1923年，随着俄国远东白俄政府的垮台，俄国舰队驶往马尼拉，他于1924年在该地退役。同年，他离开马尼拉前往哈尔滨，不久后加入为满洲军阀张作霖元帅的中国军队服务的白俄分队。他在该分队服役至1927年，退役后前往上海。1927年8月，他在上海自来水公司获得助理工程师职位，并一直任职于该公司，直至1940年11月自行辞职。

OVANESSIAN LEON AND MARKOW GEORGE-
APPLICANTS TO JOIN THE S.M.P.(SPECIALS).

Constantin Petrovich LASAREFF,Russian Emigrant,single,
of Greek-Orthodox Religion,was born on March 13th.,1910
at Nicolsk-Ussuryisk,Maritime Province,Russia.
In 1919 he,together with his parents,left Russia for
Japan and subsequently resided at Yokohama where he
received his education at the St.Joseph's College. He
left Japan for Harbin in 1925 and continued his education
at the Harbin Russian College from which he graduated in
1928. In 1929 he left Harbin for Shanghai and shortly
upon his arrival here he obtained the position of a radio
mechanic and salesman with the Eletric Service Corporation
and remained with this firm until 1934 when it was closed.
He then was employed with the American Engineering
Corporation,939 Bubbling Well Road,for about one year as
a salesman,after which he worked independently in the
same capacity for a period. In 1935-1936 he was employed
as a salesman with the Radio Equipment Co.,and in October
of 1936 joined the Victor Radio Sales Co.,as a sales
manager and remained with this firm until 1938 when he
resigned and joined the Office Appliance Co.,Ltd.,Nanking
Road where he is still employed in the capacity of a
salesman.
From 1933 to 1935 Lasareff served with the Light Gun
Battery,S.V.C. and in 1937 he joined the S.M.P.(Specials)
and served with the Specials for several months.

Israel Borisovich MAXT, Russian of Jewish origin, was born on December 20,1914 at Melitopol, South Russia. He is reported to have left Russia for China in 1924 together with his mother and after a short stay in Harbin arrived in Shanghai. From 1925 to 1929 he attended the Shanghai Jewish School, after which he is reported to have been casually working as a photographer with the Navy Y.M.C.A. in Shanghai and Chefoo for a period. From 1938 to date he has been engaged in transportation business first as a partner in the Alliance Transport Co., 55 Whangpoo Road ( 1938-1939) and later as proprietor of two motor trucks,which he hires out to various transport companies. At present the trucks are hired by the Hongkew Transportation Company ( Japanese owned ),108 Minhong Road.

Applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants Committee,Moulmein Road, and at present resides with his mother, Mrs R.M. Maxt ( divorced wife of L.M. Lifshitz ) who conducts a boarding house at 175 /9 Kiaochow Road. His elder brother S.Maxt is employed as a barber at the Navy Y.M.C.A. and his sister is the wife of Mr. S. Lenoise,British, who is reported to be in Australia at present.

SUBJECT: Alfred Robert Hogg - Candidate for

-----------------------

Alfred Robert Hogg, British, was
born on December 21st 1899 at Wenchow, South
China.

Nothing is known of his early life
but from 1916 to 1918 and from 1920 to 1934
he was employed in the firm Connabe, Eckford
& Co., merchants, at Chefoo, North China.

From March 1st 1918 to June 20th
1919 he served in H.M. Forces being gazetted
Second-Lieutenant, General List in March
1919. He was demolished in June 1919.

In addition to the above military
service, applicant was, from 31st December
1937 to 10th January 1938, Chairman and
Commandant of the Tsingtao Special Police
Force, which maintained law and order in
Tsingtao during the ten strenuous days
between the evacuation of the Chinese
Authorities and the entry of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party. For his participation
in these events, applicant was awarded the
O.B.E.

From about 1935 to February 1941
applicant was the Tsingtao agent of the
Confederation Life Association and on or
about 27th February 1941 he was transferred
to the Shanghai Office of that Insurance
Company located at 51 Canton Road.

-----------------------

阿尔弗雷德·罗伯特·霍格，英国人，
1899年12月21日生于中国南方温州。

对其早年生活一无所知，但1916年至1918年以及1920年至1934年期间，
他受雇于华北烟台的商人公司康纳比、埃克福德公司（Connabe, Eckford
& Co.）。

1918年3月1日至1919年6月20日，
他在英王陛下军队服役，1919年3月被任命为
总名单中的少尉。1919年6月退役。

除上述军役外，申请人于
1937年12月31日至1938年1月10日期间，担任
青岛特别警察部队主席兼指挥官，该部队在中国当局撤离
至日本海军陆战队进驻之间那十天艰难时期内，
维持了青岛的治安秩序。因参与这些事件，
申请人被授予大英帝国勋章（O.B.E.）。

约1935年至1941年2月，申请人担任
联邦人寿协会（Confederation Life Association）的青岛代理，
1941年2月27日左右，他被调往该保险公司位于
广东路51号的上海办事处。
